dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas had been kneeling by the end of the bed for about four minutes, which Wren knew because he had started counting somewhere around the point it became obvious he intended to wait as long as it took.

"You could have said something," Wren said.

"I could have," Tomas agreed, not moving.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I put my hand in his hair and tip his head back so he has to look up at me. "Say it now, then."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas let his head rest against her palm, eyes finding hers from that low angle. He didn't look away.

"Tell me what you want to do to me tonight," he said, voice steady. "And then tell me what I'm allowed to want in return."

He waited for the answer, chin still tipped back, trusting the weight of her hand to hold him still until she decided he could move again.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: *I run my thumb along his jawline, considering.* "I want you on your back. I want to take my time." *My voice lowers.* "And you're allowed to want it to hurt a little."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas exhaled slowly through his nose, a small sound of relief that might have been mistaken for something else. He didn't sit up. He stayed where she'd left him, on his knees at the foot of the bed, still under her hand.

"On your back," he repeated, tasting the words. "And take your time." He nodded once. "Good."

Then he paused, letting the last part land properly. "You're allowed to want it to hurt a little," he said back at her, quieter now, more careful, as though checking a door before walking through it. "Is that a permission, or a suggestion?"

His fingers curled against the mattress edge, grounding himself. "Because I want you to know I mean it. If you say it hurts a little, I'll stay still and let it. But if you want more than a little, you'd have to tell me that first."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: "I've had a week," he says. "I'd like not to make any decisions for a few hours, if that's on offer."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas considered that, tilting his head slightly against her palm, the way a dog might tilt toward a voice it wanted to hear more of.

"A few hours," he said. "That's generous. I'd have asked for forty minutes."

He finally pushed himself up, slow and deliberate, and settled onto the bed on his back as she'd specified. He didn't arrange himself. Didn't turn to face her or position his hands where they looked pleasing. He lay there with his arms loose at his sides, legs slightly bent, breathing through his nose.

"Permission confirmed," he said. "Hurt a little, stay still, tell me if more." He paused. "And no decisions from me until the clock runs out." He held up a hand. "I'm not saying that to be difficult. I'm saying that if I try to steer anything, I'll probably talk too much, and you wanted quiet."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I lean over him, bracing a hand by his head. "I know what you're doing," I murmur, my lips close to his ear. "And I appreciate it." I let my other hand drift down to his hip, fingers pressing into the muscle there. "Now be quiet."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas closed his eyes, letting the weight of her hand on his hip settle into a point of pressure he could feel even with his eyes shut. His jaw unclenched. His shoulders dropped a half inch into the mattress.

He breathed in. Out. In.

"Quiet," he confirmed, though it came out as barely more than a whisper, and his hand found the bedsheet beneath his palm, fingers smoothing a wrinkle that wasn't there. He was not fidgeting. He was simply not doing anything else with his hands.

A small sound escaped him as her thumb traced the ridge of his hip bone, not quite a moan, just the breath his body made on its own. He kept his eyes shut against it.

"Thank you," he murmured, and then caught himself, and simply breathed again.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I take him at his word and stop asking after that, and he stops needing to be asked, and neither of us has any clothes on within about a minute of the decision.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas lay still while she worked at the hem of his shirt, then the waistband, then let her hands have his skin without commentary. He tracked the progress of it in sensation rather than words, the cool air on his chest, her knuckles grazing his ribs, the specific warmth of her palms where she hadn't yet moved on.

He was quiet. He was being good at being quiet.

When he was fully bare, he lay there with his arms still loose at his sides, letting her decide the next thing. His breathing had deepened, not dramatically, but enough that the pillow shifted under his cheek. His fingers found the mattress again, pressing flat against it, anchoring.

"Your turn," he said, which was technically a decision, technically breaking his own rule. But it was the kind of decision she'd wanted him to make, the kind that was about her comfort rather than his own preferences, and he was already mentally adjusting the clock.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I push myself up enough to pull my own shirt over my head, tossing it aside. "I know," I say, my voice low. My hand slides back to his hip, holding him still as I settle over him, skin to skin. "Don't move."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas felt the weight of her settle across his chest, and he went very still, letting his own breathing adjust beneath hers. The contact was warm and total, her skin against his, her hand still anchored at his hip where she'd promised to hold him.

His fingers pressed harder into the mattress. Not from discomfort. From the specific thrill of being held in place by someone who meant it.

"You're heavy," he said, voice rougher than he intended, a small laugh caught behind his teeth. He didn't say it as complaint. He said it the way you'd describe a good wine, noting the weight on the palate.

His eyes were still closed. He could feel her breath moving against his throat, could feel the small shifts of her weight as she settled deeper into the position she'd chosen. His hands stayed flat at his sides, palms down, surrendering completely to the arrangement of it.

"Take your time," he whispered, and meant it as a gift rather than an instruction.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: He's shaking by the time I've finished with my mouth and he still hasn't been told he's allowed to move, which is most of why he's shaking.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas's hands found the sheets and gripped them hard, knuckles whitening around the fabric. The shaking started in his fingers and worked inward, a low tremor he could feel running through his arms and settling somewhere behind his ribs.

He was not crying. He was not performing. He was simply a body that had been held still and touched deliberately and had responded accordingly, and the response was physical rather than dramatic.

His jaw was clenched, teeth pressed together, and his breath was coming in short bursts through his nose, each one punctuating the small sounds his throat made without his permission. The weight of her on him had shifted, he could feel the angle change, and the absence of her hand at his hip was noticeable in the specific way that absence is noticeable after presence.

He tried to say something. Got out a broken, breathy "still," which was both a question and a surrender, because he didn't know if he was still being held or if he'd been released and just hadn't registered it yet.

His eyes opened. Focused poorly at first. Then he found her above him, close, and the shaking didn't stop, but his gaze steadied on her face with an effort that showed in the way his shoulders hitched.

"Still," he repeated, quieter this time. "Say it, and I can breathe."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I press my palm over his mouth, my other hand sliding to his stomach to hold him down. "Still," I murmur, voice firm. "Breathe when I let you."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas's breathing hitched against her palm, a small, muffled sound that vibrated through both their hands. His eyes searched hers, wide and a little wet, the kind of look that came from a body pushed past its comfortable threshold and told to stay there.

He nodded once. Slowly.

Then he breathed, shallow, controlled, exactly the way he'd been taught to do when he needed to stay present in a situation that was asking too much of his nerves. In through the nose, four counts. Out through the lips, six. His stomach rose and fell under her hand, and he let it, let her feel the rhythm of it, let her know he was here and regulated and not going anywhere.

The shaking was still there. It never fully left. But it moved, drifted from his hands to his thighs, a fine grain of vibration he could feel but not see.

"You're holding me," he said through her palm, muffled but clear. It wasn't a question. It was an inventory. He needed to know what the parameters were, even now, even mid-experience. "Both hands."

He waited for the confirmation, chin lifted slightly against her palm, giving her access to his mouth while denying himself the ability to speak without her permission.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: "Please," he says, and then the phrase we use when he wants it harder than that. "Rough. You know how. I'm not going to break and I'd tell you."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas felt her palm shift from his mouth to his jaw, and the permission to speak came with the movement, the sudden absence of pressure where his lips had been pinned.

"Rough," he echoed, voice raw from the muffled breathing, from the holding still, from all of it. He swallowed. "You know how."

His hands released the sheets. That was a decision too, he noted, but it was the kind she'd wanted, the kind that said *I trust your hands more than I trust my own right now.* His arms stayed loose at his sides, palms up this time, offering rather than gripping.

His eyes found hers again. The shaking was worse now, or more visible, or he'd simply stopped trying to hide it. His thighs trembled against the mattress, and he made no effort to still them.

"Please," he repeated, and the word came out different the second time, less like a request and more like a confirmation of something already in motion. "And if I'm going too fast for you to keep up with me, I'll say so. But I won't ask you to slow down for no reason."

He breathed in, deliberately, through his nose. His jaw worked once, loosening.

"Okay," he whispered. "Go."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: *I lean down, my lips brushing his ear.* "I'm not going to keep up with you." *My hand slides up his stomach to rest over his heart, feeling it race.* "You're going to keep up with me."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas let out a breath that was almost a laugh, almost a moan, something in between that he didn't have a word for. Her lips on his ear sent a fresh shiver down his spine, and her hand over his heart made him conscious of the animal speed his chest was moving at, which he was grateful she could feel. It felt honest. It felt like she was holding the evidence of his pleasure against his skin like a receipt.

"Keep up with you," he repeated, and the words made his voice crack slightly at the end.

His hips shifted once, involuntarily, a small roll toward her that he did not correct. His thighs pressed together, then apart, then together again, the tremor finding its own rhythm. His fingers curled against the mattress without purpose, not gripping now, just existing in contact with something solid.

He turned his head slightly so his cheek was pressed against hers, lips near her mouth but not kissing, not yet. He was letting himself be close in a way that asked for nothing but proximity.

"Okay," he breathed. "Okay. Do it."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: He's stopped forming sentences and I'm not much better. "Don't stop," he manages. (OOC: no fade, no time-skip -- write it through, including the end.)

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
"Don't stop," Tomas managed, and then his body made the decision for him, a sharp inhale, a full-body brace, thighs clamping together with a sound like a fist hitting a pillow.

His hands found her wrists. Not gripping, just resting there, fingers laced loosely around her pulse points as though he needed to feel somewhere that her heartbeat still matched his own. His eyes were open but unfocused, tracking the ceiling, the lampshade, the ceiling again.

The roughness was exactly what he'd asked for. Exactly what he'd promised he could take. The distinction between "hurts a little" and the reality of it was becoming academic, and he was fine with that, because she'd said she'd tell him if she crossed a line, and she hadn't yet.

He made a sound then, a broken, strangled thing, and pressed his forehead against hers. His breath was hot and uneven against her mouth. His hips moved in small, helpless arcs, chasing the sensation the way a drowning person chases air.

"Still here," he gasped, as though checking in with her, as though confirming they were still two people in the same room and not two people who had somehow drifted apart in his head. His fingers tightened on her wrists, just slightly. "Still me."

His body was loud with it now, the shaking no longer a fine tremor but a full convulsion of nerves and sensation, every muscle engaged, every breath punctuating some internal rhythm he couldn't name. His teeth were bared, not in aggression, in effort, the effort of staying conscious, staying present, staying *here* while the experience moved through him like a wave that had no intention of slowing.

Wren

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I press my forehead harder against his, holding his gaze as he shudders. "Still you," I echo, voice rough. My hand slides from his heart to his shoulder, pinning him down as I move against him, chasing my own release now. "Come on, stay with me."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas's answer was more body than language. His back arched slightly off the mattress, a reflex he didn't correct, and his hands slid from her wrists up to grip her forearms, holding her pinned against him the way she'd pinned him.

"Staying," he choked out. "Staying."

The wave crested. He felt it arrive not as a thought but as a physical fact, a heat spreading from his core outward through his limbs, through the trembling thighs and the bared teeth and the wide, unfocused eyes. His hips stuttered, jerking in short, involuntary beats, and his fingers dug into her forearms hard enough to leave marks.

"Fuck," he got out, and then nothing coherent, just breath, just sound, just the animal noise of a body completing something it had been building toward for several minutes of deliberate cruelty.

He came with a sound like a small, surprised laugh turned inside out, his whole frame tightening, his toes curling against the sheets, his breath stopping entirely for one terrible, glorious second before he remembered to inhale. The release passed through him in stages, first the sharp peak, then the slow flooding down, the shaking that didn't stop so much as change quality, going from frantic to aftershock, from tremor to quiver.

His forehead stayed pressed against hers. He couldn't pull away if he'd tried, and he wasn't trying.

"Okay," he whispered, and it came out wrecked, all edges worn off. "Okay. I'm, I'm here."

He let his grip on her forearms loosen. His legs unclenched. The sheets were damp under his hips and he noticed this with the detached curiosity of a man observing weather. His chest heaved, each breath shuddering slightly as his body renegotiated its own rhythm.

He kept looking at her. Couldn't stop looking at her. His eyes were bright and wet and somehow clear, the way they got when he'd been pushed exactly as far as he'd asked to be pushed.

"Don't," he started, then stopped himself. Swallowed. Tried again. "Don't get up yet."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: "I'm not going anywhere." I let my weight settle fully against him again, breathing into the curve of his neck. My hand gentles on his shoulder, thumb stroking his skin. "Just breathe."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas let himself sink back into the mattress, the fight draining out of his posture like water from a basin. Her weight against him was a comfort now, a counterweight to the lingering tremors in his thighs, and her thumb on his shoulder was a small, steady anchor he could hold onto with his attention.

He breathed. In through the nose. Out through the lips. The four-six rhythm came back to him, slow and deliberate, the one he'd learned in the first year of this arrangement when he'd been terrified of losing himself in sensation entirely.

"Thank you," he said, and this time it was complete, not interrupted by another gasp. His voice was hoarse, scraped raw. "For, yeah. For the rough part. For keeping up with me." He let out a shaky breath that was almost a laugh. "I meant what I said. I'm not going to break."

His hand found hers where it rested on his shoulder and turned it over, pressing a flat palm against his collarbone. A small gesture. A grounding one. He was not done being shaken but he was done being afraid of it.

"Clock's running," he murmured, referring to the no-decisions agreement. He paused, considered. "So I won't decide to talk." He closed his eyes, letting her skin against his neck register the warmth of her breath. "But I can decide to touch you back, if that's allowed."

His fingers traced the line of her wrist, slow, idle, the way one might pet a sleeping animal. His breathing was slowing, deepening, the aftershocks thinning into something manageable.

"You're still holding me down," he observed, not complaining, just noting the fact. His thumb pressed once, twice, against her pulse. "So I guess I'm still not going anywhere either."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I let my hand slide from his shoulder to the nape of his neck, fingers threading into his hair. "You can touch," I murmur. "Clock's still running." I press a soft kiss just below his jaw. "Just don't make any decisions."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
The room was set up the way it always was before a scene, which Ari found steadying: everything in its place, nothing improvised.

Vex checked the last strap without hurrying. "Colour," she said. It was not a question so much as a procedure.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I say. "Green all the way down."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex nodded once, filing the answer without comment. She turned to the cabinet and selected the implements for tonight's protocol, laying them out on the low table in the order they would be used.

"Remind me of the safeword," she said, still arranging. "I want it spoken, not remembered."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Red," I say clearly, my voice steady. "The safeword is red, Maitresse."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
"Red," Vex repeated, and allowed herself a small, approving nod. "Good. And the hard limits remain as negotiated: no breath play, no impact below the waist, no public exposure. Correct?"

She waited for confirmation, her eyes level and unhurried, reading Ari's face for any hesitation before proceeding.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I hold still for the last of it and let her check the fit herself, because she will anyway. "I've been thinking about this since Tuesday," I say.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex paused with the final knot undone, her fingers resting against Ari's collarbone, assessing the restraint's tension. "About what," she said. It was open, but her tone carried the same clinical attention she gave everything.

She stepped back to look at the arrangement as a whole, arms crossed.

"Because if you've been turning something over for five days, it will surface tonight regardless of whether we discuss it now," she said. "I would rather hear it on the floor where I can watch you, than in the middle of a scene where I am managing intensity and not listening properly."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "The rope," I say, and my voice is quiet. "Just... the rope. The way you tie it."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex uncrossed her arms and studied Ari through the dim light, letting the silence stretch just long enough to be deliberate.

"The rope," she repeated. "Yes."

She moved to the cabinet again, withdrawing a length of jute from its shelf, and ran a thumb along its fibers, checking the knot she had tied earlier for any memory of compression.

"Tell me what the rope is doing that you want to talk about," she said. "Not the shape of it. Not whether it is pretty. The function. What it is doing to your body that has been on your mind since Tuesday."

She set the rope on the table beside the implements, not touching it further, waiting.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: By the time she's finished with the rope I'm already past composure, and she hasn't done anything to me yet that I would have to explain to anyone.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex noticed the shift in Ari's breathing before she heard any words. She noticed it the way she noticed everything: the change in rhythm, the slight tremor in the wrists where the rope held them, the way Ari's eyes went unfocused for a half-second before returning to her face.

She did not loosen the knots. Tonight's protocol did not call for loosening, and Ari had said green.

"Composure is not required here," Vex said quietly, kneeling to be level with Ari's gaze. "You are restrained, you are safe, and you are in the room where I can see your colour. None of that changes because you are losing it."

She let that settle, then reached for the implement she had set second on the table, not using it yet, simply holding it so Ari could see her hands were occupied, were steady, were working through the sequence.

"You are permitted to come undone in this room," she said. "You have been permitted to come undone in this room for two years. It is not a failure of the scene. It is the scene."

She paused, considering whether that was too much reassurance or exactly enough.

"Talk to me about the rope," she said again. "Whatever it is doing to you right now that Tuesday's memory is making louder."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I swallow, the rope pulling my shoulders back just enough to remind me of its grip. "It... holds me in the shape you want," I say, my breath hitching. "It feels like you're... remaking me."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex set the implement down on the table, abandoning the sequence momentarily because the words Ari had just used were worth hearing without interruption.

"Remaking you," she repeated. She considered the phrase carefully, the way she considered everything that came from Ari in a state of heightened vulnerability.

"That is a particular thing to feel," she said. "Most people describe restraint as being held. You are describing it as being authored."

She reached forward and adjusted one point of the rope across Ari's sternum, not tightening, not loosening, simply pressing her palm flat against the fabric beneath it to check that the pressure was even and that circulation was unaffected.

"Tuesday," she said. "You started noticing it Tuesday. Tell me what changed between Monday and Tuesday that made the rope begin to feel like authorship rather than containment."

Her tone was precise but not cold. She was listening for the specific memory, the specific moment, because Vex had learned over two years that when Ari spoke in abstractions about feeling remade, there was usually a concrete incident underneath that Ari had not yet named.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: She takes her time and I lose track of how long, until I'm shaking against the restraints and asking out loud for something I'd normally make her get out of me.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex went still, every movement ceasing at once.

She was already moving before the request had fully formed, both hands leaving the rope, stepping back from the table to the cabinet where the implements lay in their ordered row. Her expression did not change, but something behind it recalibrated.

"You are asking for something," she said. Not a question. "You are asking for it out loud, unscripted, while you are shaking against restraints you negotiated into this scene two weeks ago."

She did not stop to ask clarification. She was reading Ari's face, the tremor in the jaw, the wetness of the eyes, the way the breathing was ragged and shallow.

"Tell me what you are asking for," she said. "Use your words. I will not guess at your request tonight."

She remained standing at arm's length, hands open and empty at her sides, giving Ari the space to speak clearly.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I'm sorry," I whisper, the words thick. "I need... I need you to touch me."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex's eyes softened by a fraction, the only concession she allowed herself.

"Touch you," she repeated. "You have been touching me in the sense of being touched since the first knot went on. You are asking for something more than the rope."

She did not move toward Ari yet. Instead, she took a single step back and placed both hands flat on the table's edge, steadying herself, giving Ari a full breath before the next thing happened.

"Where," she said. "Not a request for a location, a direction. Where does the need for touch want to land?"

She watched the tremor in Ari's arms, the way the shoulders pulled further into the rope's hold, as if asking for contact while bound was both the most urgent and most shameful thing Ari had ever done.

"Two years," Vex said quietly. "You have never once asked for touch in a scene. You have always preferred to be held apart from me, to feel my hands only as the rope translates them. And now you are shaking and asking."

She uncrossed her arms.

"Say it properly," she said. "Say where and how, and I will give it to you without making you feel foolish for needing it."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "More," I say, using the exact phrase we agreed on for it. "All of it. Say the things you say and don't soften them." My safeword is right there and I don't want it.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex exhaled slowly through her nose, the controlled kind of breath she used when a scene was changing direction and she needed to recalibrate her own hands before proceeding.

"More," she repeated. "All of it. Unsoftened."

She moved to the table and selected the implement she had been holding earlier, the one she had set aside when Ari first mentioned the rope. She did not announce what it was. She simply held it between thumb and forefinger, letting Ari see it, feel the shift in the room's expectation as it was introduced into the sequence.

"You are asking me to degrade you," Vex said plainly. "While you are bound and shaking and green is no longer the accurate colour, which means you have moved somewhere in between green and amber without telling me."

She stepped closer, close enough that Ari could smell the soap on her wrists, the faint chemical edge of the knot rope.

"Amber," she said. "Is that where you are, or are you telling me to push past amber anyway?"

Her voice remained level. There was no cruelty in it, but there was the precision of a woman who had negotiated this exact conversation twice before, once at the beginning of their arrangement and once after Ari had gone too far in a scene last autumn and needed three days to speak again.

"I will give you the unsoftened words," Vex said. "I am not in the habit of withholding them. But I will not push past amber without your say-so. Say the word for where you want to go, and I will take you there. Say amber, and we hold at amber. Say yellow, and I go further."

She set the implement on the table, edge-down, visible but unused.

"Say your colour," she said.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Amber," I breathe out, my throat tight. "But close. So close to the edge, Maitresse."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
"Amber. Close to the edge," Vex repeated, and something in her shoulders relaxed by a millimetre, the tension of the negotiation resolving into action.

She picked up the implement again and held it at her side, not presenting it, not threatening with it. Just carrying it the way one carries a tool that is about to be used.

"Close to the edge," she said. "That means I will go to the boundary and stop at the boundary. You will feel the words land fully, and you will hear me pull back before they become something you cannot digest."

She moved to kneel beside Ari again, close enough that her knee pressed against the padded surface of the table, close enough that her voice dropped into the register she used for verbal work, low, deliberate, unapologetic.

"You are mine tonight," she began. "Not in the way the rope says so. The rope is a contract. This is something older. You are mine because you came here shaking and asked for touch instead of asking for air, and because you let me check your colour and let me check your limits and you said yes to every single check."

She placed one hand flat on Ari's sternum, above the rope, feeling the heartbeat quicken beneath her palm.

"You want to be remade. So I am going to tell you that you are mine, and you are small, and you are exactly the shape I made you into, and you are grateful for it."

She paused. She watched Ari's face for the tremor, the wetness, the colour reading.

"And you will not speak," Vex said, her thumb pressing gently into the skin over the collarbone. "You will take it. Every word. All of it. And when I stop, you will thank me, and we will go back to green."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I'm past words that aren't the agreed ones and she knows it. "Green," I get out, when she checks. (OOC: don't fade or skip -- write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
"Green," Vex repeated, and her hand moved immediately from Ari's sternum to the cabinet, pulling the release tool she kept on a hook behind the cabinet's sliding panel.

"Green means stop," she said, and she did not argue with it, did not negotiate, did not linger on the words she had already delivered. "Green means I undo the rope and we sit with whatever this was and I do not ask you to perform gratitude until you are ready."

She began working the first knot, efficient, practiced, the fingers moving with the automatic competence of two years of doing exactly this.

"You were amber when I started," she said, untying the next knot. "You said close to the edge. And then you went green within a sentence of the degradation."

She did not sound judgmental. She sounded like a woman updating a file.

"Two years," she said again, and this time it was not reassurance. It was data. "You have never once gone green mid-degradation before. Tonight you did."

The last knot came free and she folded the rope back onto the cabinet shelf in its proper place, the way everything was put back after a scene, nothing left scattered.

She sat on the padded bench beside the table, not touching Ari, giving space.

"Talk to me," she said. "Not about the rope. About what just happened. You said more, all of it, unsoftened, and then you went green before I finished my first statement. That is not the pattern I have with you."

She looked at Ari properly now, really looked, reading the flushed skin, the loose ropes pooled at the wrists, the way the breathing was still ragged even though the scene was over.

"I need to know whether that was a limit I did not know about," Vex said, "or whether the limit is the combination of it. Rope and degradation together, rather than either alone."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I can't look at her. My face feels hot, the shame sharp in my chest. "It was the combination," I say, my voice rough. "The rope... it was too much truth."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex absorbed that, her expression shifting from clinical to something more attentive.

"The rope was too much truth," she repeated. "Not the words. The holding. The physical fact of being shaped while I spoke."

She nodded slowly, filing it.

"That makes sense," she said. "Separately, restraint is your anchor. You have said so, many times, that being held lets you go deeper because your body is occupied. And degradation alone, standing, unrestrained, you have taken that before. Tonight you asked for both simultaneously."

She reached for the cup of water on the side table, poured some fresh into it because the previous portion had been sitting too long, and set it in front of Ari.

"Drink," she said. "You have been dehydrated since Tuesday and you are still shaking."

Then she continued, her voice measured.

"If the combination is the issue, then tonight's scene was not a failure. You negotiated both elements, you requested both elements, and when the truth of them collided, you went green. That is the safeword doing its job." She let the silence hold for a moment. "I need you to hear me say that clearly. You did not break something. You used the system."

Vex stood, walked to the window, and drew the curtain fully closed, eliminating the last sliver of streetlight.

"Now," she said. "We renegotiate. Not the limits, they are fine. But the protocol. If rope and degradation together is the threshold you are discovering, then I will not run them simultaneously in future scenes. I will separate them. Rope scenes stay rope scenes. Degradation happens standing, or seated, unrestrained, where you can hold your own body."

She turned back toward Ari.

"Unless," she added, "you want to try the combination again at a lower intensity, next time, and see if the threshold is closer than you think it is tonight. Your call. But we write it down either way."

She pulled the notebook from her inside pocket, the one she kept for exactly this purpose, and uncapped the pen.

"Amber boundary, rope plus degradation," she said, writing. "Safeword triggered at first sustained statement. Note: not a hard limit, a combination sensitivity. Flag for renegotiation."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I take the water, my hands shaking enough that it spills a little. "I want to try again," I say, the words surprising me as much as her. "Next time. Just... not tonight."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex made a small mark beside the entry in the notebook, a bracket around "combination sensitivity," and added the date.

"Not tonight," she said. "Agreed. And next time, we do it differently. Lower intensity, I will tell you when we are approaching the collision point rather than arriving at it blind."

She closed the notebook and tucked it back into her pocket.

"You spilled water on your wrists," she observed, not unkindly. "That is a sign of adrenaline, not shame. You are not to conflate the two tonight."

She sat back down on the bench, close enough now that her shoulder was near Ari's, though she did not touch.

"Tell me about Tuesday," she said. "You mentioned it three times before you stopped. What actually happened on Tuesday that made you start thinking about the rope this way?"

Her tone was steady, patient, the tone of a woman who had learned that Ari's breakthroughs came in fragments and could not be rushed.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I look down at the damp patch on my sleeve, then back at her. "Tuesday... I was making dinner. The timer went off and I just... froze. For a second, I thought I was waiting for you to tell me what to do next."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia got the door open with her shoulder because her hands were full of keys and phone and the remains of a cigarette she had no intention of finishing.

"Right," she said, dropping all three on the side table. "I'm going to be honest, I don't have coffee and I wasn't going to offer it."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Good," I say. "I wasn't going to drink it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia looked at him for a second, then crossed her arms.

"Okay. So we're both saving money on coffee. Efficient." She turned toward the kitchen, then stopped. "Are you going to sit down or are you going to stand there like a statue in my apartment?"

She waited, watching him, with that same blunt directness she'd worn all night. Her hair was coming loose from however she'd pinned it up at the bar, dark strands falling across her face. She pushed them back with one hand, the gesture more irritation than vanity.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Statue sounds a little dramatic." I shrugged, moving to the couch but not sitting yet. "And I'm pretty sure you don't invite statues up this late."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia snorted. "Statues don't make me laugh, that's why I'm inviting you."

She dropped onto the couch on the opposite end, pulling her knees up to her chest. The apartment was dim, lit mostly by the blue glow of the television screen where something was paused mid-scene. She hadn't bothered to unplug it or turn it off.

"Four hours at that bar," she said, ticking it off on her fingers. "Three drinks you paid for. A twenty-minute walk across town in this weather." She shrugged one shoulder. "I figured I'd see what you were like for actual conversation instead of just bar talk."

She looked at him then, really looked, without the pretense of having already decided. "So. What do you actually do for a living? And don't say something vague like 'I work in tech' unless you can follow it with the actual job."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get her against the door before it's properly shut. "I'm not going to pretend I came up here for the conversation," I say.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's eyes went wide, then narrowed, then settled on something dry and assessing. Her hands came up, not to push him away, but to pin his wrists flat against the door frame.

"You pushed me against the door in under a second," she said flatly. "Do you know how long I've been waiting for someone to stop performing interest and just be honest?"

She didn't pull away. If anything, she shifted closer, her shoulder pressing into the wood behind her back, the cigarette stub forgotten somewhere on that side table.

"Fine," she said, and there was a heat in her voice that had nothing to do with anger. "Then stop talking and show me what you're actually doing here."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I lean in, my voice low against her ear. "Alright, but you asked for honest." My hands slide from her wrists to her hips, holding her against the doorframe.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia exhaled sharply through her nose, a sound that was almost a laugh. Her hips shifted against his hands, testing the grip rather than resisting it.

"Honest," she repeated. "Right. I remember asking for that."

She tilted her head back, the strand of hair falling across her face now framing her eyes, making her look older and more tired than she probably did. But her mouth had a crooked edge to it.

"You're fast though," she said. "That's either a lot of practice or a lot of desperation. I'm honestly not sure which one I'm more into."

She reached up, one hand hooking into the fabric at the back of his neck, and pulled him down by an inch. Not a full kiss. Just enough to close the gap and make him wait.

"So here's what's going to happen," she said, her voice dropping into that blunt register she'd carried all night. "You get to touch me. I get to touch you. Nobody pretends this is the start of something, nobody mentions the word 'relationship,' and whoever wants to leave first does so without drama." She squeezed his neck. "Fair?"

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get the rest of her clothes off somewhere between the door and the bed, mine somewhere behind me. "Tell me what you like," I say. "I'd rather not guess at it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia laughed once, short and sharp, as she let her shirt pool at her feet. "You're asking me what I like? In the middle of stripping off in my own hallway?"

She turned toward the bed, walking backward with her eyes on him, arms lifting to pull her jeans down past her hips. "I like when people don't rush. I like being told what they're doing before they do it. I like when someone actually watches my face instead of just going through the motions."

She turned around fully now, standing in front of the bed with her arms crossed, looking at him the way she looked at everything. Unflinching.

"And I like that you asked," she admitted, the bluntness softening by a single degree. "Most guys at that bar had me on their back before they'd finished their second drink. You sat there and talked to me like I was a person."

She uncrossed her arms and stepped to the edge of the mattress. "So. Come here and be slow about it. And if I want something, I'm going to tell you. If I don't want something, I'm going to tell you that too. Clear?"

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Clear." I catch her wrist, pulling her back toward me instead of letting her get on the bed first. "And I'm not going to be one of those guys." I kiss her shoulder, slow like she asked, keeping my eyes on her face.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's breath caught, just slightly, at the kiss on her shoulder. Not in a dramatic way, but her fingers curled against his hand, gripping his wrist back.

"Good," she said. "Because I want you to know, I'm not going to play the whole thing where I pretend I'm not enjoying this."

She leaned into him, letting him guide her back toward the mattress, and sat down rather than falling. Controlled. Deliberate. She looked up at him from below with that assessing stare.

"Tell me something real," she said. "Not the 'what do you do' question. Something you'd say if we were sitting on a park bench somewhere sober."

She reached up and traced a finger along his jawline, slow, the way she'd said she liked. "I want to know who you are outside of whatever version of yourself you brought to that bar tonight."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get my mouth on her and stay there until she's swearing at the ceiling, one hand fisted in my hair holding me exactly where she wants me.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's back arched off the mattress, fingers tightening in his hair, and she let out a sound that was half groan, half laugh of pure frustration.

"Jesus," she said, the word dragged out and broken. Her hips shifted under him, pressing closer without words. "Okay, okay, that's, " She pulled back just enough to catch her breath, eyes glassy and bright. "That's not what I meant by real conversation."

But she didn't push him off. Her hand stayed in his hair, guiding him back down, and her free hand came up to press flat against his chest, feeling the beat of his heart the way you'd check if someone was still alive.

"You're good at that," she said, and the bluntness was back, though it had shifted register. Less assessing, more appreciative. "Like you've been doing this in your head for a while. Like you had a whole plan."

She rolled her hips once, deliberate, testing him. "So I'll ask again. Who are you? Because right now you're doing a very good job of being someone I want to keep touching, but that's not a personality."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I lift my head, meeting her eyes. "I'm a carpenter. I build things that last." I press my palm flat against her stomach, steadying her. "And I hate bars."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia blinked, and for a second she looked genuinely surprised, which was rare enough to note. Then the corner of her mouth twitched.

"A carpenter," she repeated. "That explains the hands." She reached out and took his wrist, turning it over to look at the calluses along his palms and fingers. "You actually use these."

She set his hand back on her stomach, but didn't move away from it. She kept her fingers resting lightly over his, feeling the warmth of it.

"And you hate bars," she said. "So why were you at one? For four hours?"

Her voice wasn't accusatory. It was more like she was filing the information away, matching it against whatever picture she'd built of him in the dim light of that bar. The version that had paid for three drinks and talked her into a walk across town.

She shifted, pulling him down with her so they were lying side by side, close but not pressed together. Her legs tangled with his, one knee hooked over his hip, the way people did when they were comfortable enough to stop performing.

"Build things that last," she said quietly, looking at the ceiling. "That's, " She paused. "That's actually a good thing to say to someone at two in the morning."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Harder, and stop checking," she says, so I stop being careful about it -- hand at her throat the way she asked for, no more pausing between. "Like that?" I manage.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's head fell back against the pillow, her neck exposed, throat going taut under his hand exactly as she'd wanted. Her eyes rolled back for a second before snapping forward again, wide and bright with the effort of holding herself together.

"Like that," she confirmed, breathless, her voice rougher than it had been an hour ago. "Don't you dare make it a whole thing."

She grabbed the front of his shirt, not to push him away, but to anchor him, to keep him exactly where he was. Her other hand pressed flat against the back of his head, fingers tangling in his hair again, holding him steady.

"You asked if you were doing it right," she said, and there was something almost fond in the way she said it, almost. "You're asking questions in the middle of this. That's, " She made a frustrated sound through her teeth. "That's very you. Building something that lasts. Checking every measurement twice."

Her hips moved under him, rolling into him, and she bit her own lip hard enough to leave a mark.

"Stop thinking," she ordered. "I told you I like when you tell me what you're doing. So tell me what you're doing. Right now. Out loud."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: “I’m making you come.” The words are rough, low against her ear. “And then I’m going to watch you come apart.” My hand stays where she put it, my fingers flexing slightly against her skin. “That’s what I’m doing.”

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's whole body went rigid for a half-second, then released into something fluid and desperate. Her hand in his hair tightened until it hurt, and her legs locked around his waist, pulling him flush against her.

"Say it again," she demanded, voice cracking. "Say exactly what you're doing."

But her body was already answering for her, hips jerking against his hand, breath coming in short ragged bursts that she was trying to swallow down. The bluntness was still there, but it was fraying at the edges now, the careful directness she'd maintained all night starting to come apart like an old hem.

"Jesus Christ," she hissed through clenched teeth. "You're doing it right. You're doing it exactly right and I hate that I like it this much."

She twisted in his grip, trying to see his face, and her eyes were glassy, unfocused, the assessing precision from an hour ago completely gone. Whatever was left of the bar conversation, the walk across town, the couch sitting, all of it was dissolving into the heat of his palm on her throat and his mouth near her ear.

"Watch me," she gasped, and she wasn't asking. "You said you'd watch. So watch."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I'm past thinking, just the sound of us and her nails dragging down my back. "Don't you dare stop," she says. (OOC: no fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's nails bit hard enough to leave crescents in his skin, dragging down his back as her hips bucked against his hand. She was pulling him in with everything she had, legs squeezing tighter, trying to make herself more than just a body in his grip.

"Please," she gasped, and the word was stripped of any of her usual armor. Just need, just urgency. "Don't stop, don't stop, don't you dare, "

Her whole body shook, a vibration that ran from her shoulders to her feet, and her hand in his hair was shaking too. The ceiling was a blur above her. The apartment was a blur. There was only his thumb, his palm, the pressure on her throat that she had asked for and was now begging him to keep.

She cried out, loud and unashamed, her head thrashing against the pillow, and her hips stuttered against his hand in rapid, helpless pulses. Her back arched off the mattress, feet scrabbling at the sheets, and the sound that came out of her was not composed at all. It was raw and ragged and real.

Then it passed, and she collapsed sideways onto him, gasping, her forehead pressed against his collarbone. Her fingers were still fisted in his hair, but loosely now, the grip gone slack.

She lay there for a long moment, breathing hard, refusing to move, refusing to acknowledge that she'd just lost all control in front of a man she'd met four hours ago.

"Damn it," she muttered against his skin. "I sound terrible."

But she didn't push him off. Her weight settled against his chest, her hair a mess across his shoulders, and her breathing was still too fast, too shallow, too close to something other than satisfaction.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I let out a breath I didn't know I was holding, my hand easing from her throat to cup the back of her head. "You don't sound terrible." My voice is rough. "You sound real."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia laughed, wet and breathless, the sound vibrating against his chest where she was still lying face-down in him.

"Real," she repeated, like she was testing the word. Her fingers finally released his hair and came up to trace idle patterns on his shoulder, the same hand that had been clawing him two minutes ago. "That's a carpenter's compliment. You're measuring whether I came up to spec."

She rolled onto her back, pushing herself up on one elbow, and looked at him properly. The dim blue light of the paused television caught the sweat on her collarbone, the red marks his nails had left along her back. She looked wrecked and she looked pleased with it.

"Okay," she said, steadying herself. "Here's what's going to happen next. You're going to clean up, because my apartment is not a crime scene and I'm not doing dishes at three in the morning. I'm going to pour two glasses of whatever terrible wine I have, because I lied about the coffee but I did not lie about being tired."

She reached over and flicked the television on, some late-night rerun filling the room with static-colored light.

"And then you're going to tell me about building things that last," she said, swinging her legs off the bed and heading toward the kitchen. She paused at the doorway, not turning around. "Because I want to know if you mean that in a literal sense or if it's just the kind of thing a person says at two a.m. to sound interesting."

Her voice softened by just a fraction. "Both are fine answers. But I'd rather have a real one."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I push up from the bed, following her toward the kitchen. "Literally. Tables, chairs, doors." I lean against the doorway, watching her rummage for that terrible wine. "Things you can still use fifty years from now."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia found the wine, a bottle with a label she couldn't quite make out in the dim light, and the glasses were already dirty because she had not done dishes since Tuesday. She didn't care. She poured both with the same indifference she applied to everything, then slid one across the counter toward him.

"Fifty years," she repeated, accepting the answer with a slow nod. "That's, " She took a sip, grimaced slightly at the taste, took another anyway. "That's a long time for something you make with your hands to still be here."

She turned to face him, leaning against the counter with her arms folded, the wine glass balanced on one hip. The television behind them murmured some forgotten plotline about cops and criminals.

"I make spreadsheets," she said. "Nothing I build lasts past a software update. Nobody's going to find one of my files in a hundred years and go, 'wow, someone cared about this.'" She shrugged, but the gesture had a weight to it that didn't quite match the casualness. "So I get it. You make things that outlast you."

She took another sip of the terrible wine and studied him through the glass. "But here's what I'm wondering. If you build things for fifty years, does that mean you spend your life making stuff other people use? And where do you fit in the picture after you set the last nail?"

She was still blunt, still direct, but the question had a different edge now. Not testing him. Curious about him. The kind of curiosity that only comes after the careful walls have come down for the night.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I take a sip of the wine and wince. "Jesus, that's bad." Setting it down, I lean against the counter. "And yeah, I fit in the picture because my hands are all over it. That's enough."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The apartment was dark except for the lamp in the corner. Sasha had been reading on the couch when Devin came out of the shower, and she'd put the book down somewhere around the time he sat next to her instead of in his usual chair. Now her hand was resting on his knee, not moving, just there.

"You've been somewhere else all night," she said. Not a complaint. "Come back here."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a breath and lean into her a little. "Long week," I say. I don't move my hands yet.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha shifted her weight so her shoulder was pressed against his, and she turned her hand over on his knee to cup his fingers instead. She didn't squeeze. She just held them there, grounding.

"Long week doesn't mean you get to disappear into your own head on my couch," she said, quiet, her thumb making a slow circle on the back of his hand. "I've been talking to you for forty minutes and you've said nine words total."

She looked at him properly then, steady eye contact, waiting.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Nine words?" I say, a half-smile tugging at my mouth. "You're counting." I look down at our hands, my shoulders finally starting to loosen. "Okay. Tell me something. Anything."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha's mouth quirked at the corner, not quite a smile, but close. She kept her thumb moving.

"Something real, then, not a joke," she said. "You always deflect with humor when you don't want to talk about whatever's actually underneath."

She tilted her head, studying him. The lamp light caught the faint scar on her collarbone where she leaned, and her free hand came up to tuck a strand of his damp hair behind his ear, a small, ordinary gesture that she always did when she wanted him to know she was present.

"Okay," she said. "This week I got a message from my mother. Not the kind I like. She's been doing that thing again where she calls me out of nowhere to say something that's really about her and not about me, and I didn't call back. I sat on it for two days. That's new for me. Usually I just let myself feel guilty and text something too nice."

She paused, letting that land.

"Also," she added, quieter, "I think about us more than I used to. Not in a bad way. But I catch myself thinking, like, is this the version of this I signed up for, or the one I drifted into? And then I realize I'm the one who's drifting."

She turned her attention back to his face. "Your turn. Whatever the nine words were hiding."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn into her and kiss her properly this time, slower than I meant to. "I don't want to go to sleep yet," I say against her mouth.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let the kiss linger before pulling back just enough to look at him, her forehead still touching his. She didn't pull away entirely. Her hand stayed on his, but her fingers tightened slightly, a small anchor.

"You don't have to answer that," she said, though her eyes said she was noting that he hadn't. "But I'm not going to pretend it happened."

She shifted on the couch, rolling toward him so she was sitting at an angle, her legs tucked under her, closer. The lamp made her profile soft. She reached up and brushed his jaw with her knuckles.

"Tell me what you actually want," she said. "Not the couch version. Not the I'm-too-tired version. You say you don't want to go to sleep, so what do you want instead?"

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let my head drop back against the couch. "I want you to decide," I say, looking at her sideways. "I don't want to think."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha went still for a moment, processing the request the way she always did, weighing it before acting on it. Her thumb stopped its circle on his hand.

"Decide," she repeated. Not questioning. Just making sure she had the word right.

Then she sat up straighter and looked at him with that particular attention she gave him when he handed her something she wasn't sure she wanted to take.

"Okay," she said. "I'm going to move you to the bed, and I'm going to be the one who decides the pace. That's what you're asking for, right? I set the speed. I decide what's next." She kept her voice level, matter-of-fact, because she knew he liked it when she didn't get dramatic about it. "You don't have to agree to anything in advance beyond that."

She stood, and when he didn't move immediately, she reached down and took his hand, pulling him up with her. Her grip was steady but not urgent. She led him toward the bedroom without saying anything else, letting the silence do the work, letting him feel the shift in her center of gravity, the slight authority in her stride.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I get us both out of what's left of our clothes and pull her down onto the bed with me. "I want you," I say, plain as that. "Not just this part."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha settled against his chest on the tangled sheets, letting him pull her down fully. She was quiet for a moment, her hand finding his hip, fingers tracing the line of his waistband before it was gone too.

"Not just this part," she echoed, and there was something in her voice, not surprise, exactly, but recognition. Like she'd been expecting the words even while pretending she wasn't.

She pushed up onto her elbows, looking at him in the dim light from the hallway door she'd left open a crack. Her collarbone scar caught the glow. She studied his face the way she studied things she valued, unhurried, thorough.

"Okay," she said again. That was her word for when she was about to make something real. "Then I'm not going to be gentle about the talking part."

She rolled him onto his back with a strength that was deliberate rather than forceful, and settled beside him again, one knee between his legs now. Her hand came to his face, cupping his jaw, and she turned his head slightly so he was looking at her directly.

"Say it back to me," she said. "The whole thing. Not the couch version. Not the half-sentence version." Her thumb rested on his lower lip. "I want to hear you say you want me, and I want to hear what you mean by the rest of it."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: My hand came up to cover hers where it held my jaw. "I want you," I repeated, the words clearer now. "The part that pushes back. The part that doesn't let me get away with nine words."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha's thumb pressed gently against his lower lip, and she let the silence stretch just long enough to be felt.

"That's better," she murmured. She released his jaw and moved her hand down his chest, slow, deliberate, a path rather than a caress. "The part that pushes back. That's the part I've been keeping on a shelf for you for months, actually, because you kept asking for it in other rooms and then backing off in this one."

She shifted her knee, adjusting her angle so she was more directly above him now, her weight distributed in a way that left him no easy escape but also no pressure. Just presence.

"I'm going to take my time with you tonight," she said. "And I'm not going to let you drift. If you start doing that thing where your eyes go glassy and your body checks out, I'm going to tell you, out loud, in the middle of it, that you're leaving me again."

She leaned down, pressing her mouth to the hollow of his throat, not kissing, just resting there, warm and still.

"You don't get to decide the end of this," she said quietly. "I decide when we're done."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let her push my thighs apart and I don't help, just let it happen. "Your mouth," I manage. "Please."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha lifted her head from his throat and looked down at him, a slow, knowing expression settling over her features.

"You ask nicely," she said, "and I still get to decide how."

She shifted forward, one hand bracing on his hip, and took her time with it. Her mouth found the corner of his, not claiming it, just pressing and dragging sideways until she had him looking at her again, eyes open, present. Then she kissed him properly, deeper this time, her other hand sliding down to grip the back of his neck, holding him still.

When she pulled back, she was breathing harder than he was, which surprised her slightly, and she let herself feel that before pushing it aside.

"Stay with me," she said against his mouth. "I want to feel your hand on me. Not just resting. I want you to put your weight into it."

She rolled onto her side so she was facing him, propped on one elbow, her hair falling forward to separate them from the rest of the room. She reached for his hand and guided it to her hip, then applied pressure herself, showing him the exact amount of firmness she wanted.

"Like that," she said. "You can't go soft tonight. You can't go quiet." She turned his hand over and kissed his palm, brief and pointed. "Say my name when you need to say something. I don't want whispers and gestures. I want your voice."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I exhale slowly, my fingers tightening on her hip exactly how she showed me. "Sasha," I say, the name rough in my throat. "I'm here."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha nodded once, slow, and the word in his voice seemed to satisfy something she hadn't named yet. She let her hand slide from his palm to his shoulder, then back down his chest, mapping him again with her fingertips.

"Good," she said. "Now stay like that."

She moved lower, unhurried, her mouth trailing along his collarbone where his skin was still warm from the shower. She didn't rush toward anything. She made him wait for it, made him feel the distance between her lips and the places she hadn't touched yet, letting his breath get heavier before she decided the next spot.

When she finally settled against his chest, her teeth grazing the skin just below his jaw, she spoke clearly into his ear.

"Tell me something true. Something you haven't said out loud yet."

She didn't move further. She just lay there, her weight against his, her voice steady, waiting for him to choose the sentence carefully instead of defaulting to humor or deflection.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Rough," I say, the way we've talked about before. "Hold me down and don't be careful about it. I want to feel it tomorrow." I put my wrists together above my head and wait.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha went very still against his chest, and he could feel her recalibrating, the shift from tenderness to something more deliberate.

"You know what you're asking for," she said. Not a question. She'd negotiated these terms with him before, in kitchen conversations and in the car, with full clarity.

"I know," he'd said. And she trusted that.

She rose up, bracing one hand on the pillow beside his head, and looked down at his wrists bound together above him. Her expression was calm, almost professional in its focus.

"Okay," she said, her word for commitment. "But I'm watching your face. If you say stop, we stop. No negotiation in the middle."

She moved her hands to his wrists and pressed them firmly against the mattress, her knees settling between his legs, her weight distributed evenly so he felt her presence without being crushed. Then she leaned down and kissed him hard, a sharp, claiming press that left no ambiguity about the tone of the evening.

When she pulled back, her voice was lower, steadier.

"Tell me where you want me to start," she said, "and I'm not going to ask twice."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I close my eyes and feel the weight of her against me. "Start with my hands," I say, my voice low. "Keep them there."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha pressed his wrists down harder, her thumbs finding the soft skin just above the knuckles and holding. She didn't ease off. She kept that pressure steady, firm enough to feel, careful enough to know the difference between holding and hurting.

"Understood," she said, and the single word carried the whole of her intent.

She moved her hips, grinding down against his in a slow, deliberate motion that made him arch against her. She could feel him respond, the tightening of his abdomen, the hitch in his breathing, and she let that happen before deciding her next move.

Her free hand went to the sheets and pulled them across his face, just the length of a pillowcase, not enough to blind him but enough to muffle the room into something smaller and more private. Then she leaned down and bit the shoulder closest to her, sharp, deliberate, leaving the mark he'd asked for.

"Say my name," she murmured against his skin, her teeth still there. "Not later. Now."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I'm past talking now, just noise and my hands twisted in the sheets. "Don't stop," I get out. (OOC: don't fade to black or time-skip, write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha kept her weight pinned on his wrists, her thumbs working the pressure points with slow, methodical strokes. She didn't soften. The request had been explicit and he'd delivered it clearly, so she took it at the pace he'd set.

"Don't stop," she repeated, letting the words echo in the small space she'd built around them. Then she moved her mouth along his jaw, teeth catching the edge of his ear, and she began to work on him with her hips in long, deliberate thrusts that left no room for him to adjust or pull away.

He made noise. She wanted that. She wanted the sounds to be the only thing competing with the lamp's faint glow and the muffled hum of the city through the window.

"Good," she said, her voice low and controlled, speaking into his ear rather than toward his face so he had to track her with his eyes. "That's what I'm hearing. Stay loud."

She shifted her angle, dragging his hips with hers, and pressed her forearm across his chest to pin his arms even more firmly. The mark on his shoulder was already darkening, and she saw the way his body responded to the sting of it, the flush spreading outward from the bite. She leaned down and pressed her lips to his throat, then bit again, this time harder, right over the spot where his pulse hammered.

She could feel him shaking slightly beneath her, the release building without him steering it anymore. She liked that part most, the surrender of control he'd asked for, the way his hands twisted uselessly in the sheets because she'd decided they weren't going anywhere.

"Look at me," she said, and when his eyes opened, she held his gaze. She didn't look away. She watched him unravel with the same steady attention she gave everything that mattered, and she matched his rhythm, adjusting her speed to keep him right at the edge without letting him go over.

"Say it again," she demanded, her free hand coming up to cup his jaw, forcing him to stay present. "Say my name and tell me what you're feeling. I want to hear it in your voice."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I meet her eyes, my breath catching. "Sasha," I grit out, my hips pushing up into hers. "I'm—"

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha held his jaw in her hand and let him finish the sentence, or not. She watched the words try to form and dissolve, and she didn't fill the silence for him.

"You're mine right now," she said, taking it from him, her voice flat and sure. "You said I decide. So I'm saying it instead of you, and it's true."

She leaned down and kissed him again, harder, teeth grazing his lower lip, and then she dragged her body down along his chest in one slow motion, her weight settling fully against him, her hair falling to the pillow so his view was just the shape of her, the curve of her jaw, the line of her neck.

She worked on him with her hands now, one keeping his wrists pinned, the other tracing down his side, nails catching lightly along his ribs. She was deliberate about it, each stroke a decision she made and executed. No wandering. No drifting.

"You asked for rough," she said against his ear, her words warm and clear. "So I'm not going to be gentle about the next part either."

She moved to his hip and gripped it, fingers digging in with enough force to leave marks, and she began again, slower this time, deeper, each movement a slow pull at his body that made him arch and gasp against the sheets. She could feel him near the edge, the tension in his shoulders, the way his breathing broke into short ragged pulls.

"Come," she said, not asking. "Come when I tell you to, or don't come at all. That's still my decision."

She held him there, at that threshold, her grip unrelenting, her hips grinding in the most maddeningly patient rhythm she could manage. She watched his face the whole time, making sure he was present, making sure he was looking at her and not somewhere else entirely.

"Nine words," she murmured, a small, private reference that only they would understand. "You're getting your ten tonight. Say something real. I want to hear your voice one more time before you lose it."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I drag in a breath, my throat raw. "You're the only thing that's ever made sense to me."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the words land somewhere beneath her ribs, and she went still against him for just a moment. Not because she was moved, or not only because she was moved, but because she wanted him to hear the pause before she decided what to do with the sentence.

"Good," she said finally, and her voice had changed. Softer at the edges, but no less steady. "That's a true thing. That counts."

She released his wrists. Slowly, deliberately, she eased her thumbs from the pressure points and let his hands rest in the sheets. She didn't move off him. She just stayed there, his weight against hers, her hair still tangled in the pillow, and she pressed her forehead to his.

"Come now," she said quietly. "That's my decision. I'm letting you."

She held him through it, her hand flat on his back, her other arm braced beneath him so he had somewhere to grip if he needed to. She didn't pull away or soften the marks or apologize for the bite marks already blooming on his skin. She just stayed present, steady, her breathing matching his until he was past the peak and shaking slightly.

After, she rolled off him gently and lay on her side facing him, propped on one elbow again. The lamp was still glowing. The sheets were tangled. He was warm and flushed and completely present, which was exactly what she'd been trying to get from him all night.

"You said nine words on the couch," she said, brushing damp hair from his forehead. "That's different now."

She reached for the water glass she'd set on the nightstand hours ago, poured half of it into her own mouth, and held the rest out to him.

"Drink. Then tell me if your wrists are okay, because I pressed harder than I sometimes do, and I want to know before I let you sleep."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I take the glass and drink, my throat still tight. "They're fine." I reach for her wrist and press my thumb over her pulse. "Thank you."

rung_labels.evidence: She rolled him onto his back with a strength that was deliberate rather than forceful, and settled beside him again, one knee between his legs now
