dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun had planned to say something when the door opened. He had in fact planned several things, over roughly nineteen weeks, and had rehearsed at least two of them.

Halle got the door open and he forgot all of them.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I don't say any of the things I planned either. I drop the bag and close the distance.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun's hands come up fast, catching Halle's shoulders, then sliding down to their hips, then gripping tight enough that the fingers leave marks. He smells like airplane air and hotel soap and something underneath both that Jun recognizes as the specific exhaustion of a person who has been on a plane for eight hours and hasn't slept properly in five months.

"You look good," Jun says, because he is thirty-three years old and apparently still cannot say the obvious thing. "You look really good. Did you eat today? Did you sleep?"

He is kissing them hard, tasting salt, tasting whatever coffee they'd grabbed before coming out here. His forehead presses against theirs when he pulls back, and his eyes are wet in a way that is entirely disproportionate to the situation.

"God," he says. "Five months. I counted them. I counted the days in between, which is stupid, but I did it." He laughs, a short broken sound. "I brought you something. I left it in the car because I wasn't sure you'd want it and then I thought, what if you didn't want to be here, what if you were angry, what if I came home and you were angry and I'd already spent the money on the thing I thought you'd like."

He is talking too fast. He knows he is talking too fast. He pulls Halle in again, pressing their whole body against his, and mumbles into their hair, "I'm sorry I'm a mess. I'm not a mess. This is good. I'm not a mess about this."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I pull back just enough to look at him, my own eyes stinging. "You're a beautiful mess," I say, voice thick. Then I kiss him again, slower this time, my hands framing his face. "I'm not angry. I'm just...so tired of waiting."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun's hands slide from Halle's hips up to their face, mirroring the gesture, and he kisses them back with a tenderness that contradicts everything from the last ninety seconds. His thumbs trace the line of their cheekbones.

"Tired of waiting," he repeats, and the words land somewhere heavy in his chest. "Yeah. Me too."

He pulls back just enough to look at them properly, really look, the way he hadn't in the first wave of relief. His gaze moves over their face like he's memorizing it again, updating the file. A little weight lost. A scar he doesn't recognize on their jawline, faint, maybe a month old.

"You cut yourself?" he asks, and then sounds annoyed at himself. "No, wait. Don't answer that. Tell me about it later. Tell me about everything later."

He presses his forehead to theirs again, breathing them in. The hotel soap is still on him, but underneath it is his own smell, his own skin, the one they've known for six years.

"I missed you in a way that made me do something embarrassing on the flight," he says quietly. "I called your mother three times. Not because she was worried, because she was worried, but also because I wanted to hear someone say your name out loud. She said you'd been fine. She said you'd been working too much. She said you should come pick me up, which I did, obviously, because I wasn't driving a rental car in my sleep."

A shaky laugh. He kisses the corner of their mouth, then their temple, then back to their lips.

"I brought you the thing," he says, finally remembering. "It's in the car. It's stupid, probably. It's the stupid thing I bought off some website at two in the morning when I couldn't sleep and was thinking about what you'd like. But it's there, and I want you to have it, and I want you to tell me if it's stupid so I can be appropriately mortified."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I kiss her and keep kissing her and we don't manage to get further into the flat than the hallway for a while.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun laughs against their mouth, the sound turning into a wet, breathless thing as he tangles his fingers in the back of their hair and pulls them closer. He is clumsy with them in the best possible way, hips meeting theirs, bodies working out the geometry of the hallway in a manner that should be funny if either of them could think about anything else.

"Okay," he manages between kisses, pressing his nose to the hollow of their throat. "Okay. That's, yeah."

He does manage to walk them backward, though, one hand on their hip, the other braced against the wall as they inch toward the living room. He keeps kissing them the entire time, tasting coffee and salt and the faint bitterness of a long day.

"I didn't know if you were going to be okay with that," he says, not really a question, just a confession he needs out. "When I left. When I was getting on the plane. I thought, what if they're not, what if five months changes things, what if I come back and we're two people who used to know each other and now we just have a shared history and a lease."

His voice cracks on the last part. He swallows it down and kisses their jaw instead.

"I'm not going anywhere," he says, firm, grounding himself in the words like they might float away too. "And I'm not going to be perfect about it. I'm going to be needy and touchy and probably ask you questions about your day that I've already asked you twice because I can't remember the answers."

He reaches the living room and finally stops, though not because he's satisfied with the distance between them. Because he's out of wall.

"There's food in the fridge," he offers, gesturing vaguely behind him. "I made lasagna when I got home. Or I think I made lasagna. It's in the oven, or it was, I got distracted by the idea of you being here."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I laugh, a little breathless, and lean into him. "You made lasagna? While you were waiting for me? That's...god, I love you." I take his face in my hands. "And I'm not going anywhere either. Now, about that stupid thing in the car..."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun exhales a laugh, pressing his whole face into their palms like he's trying to be swallowed by their hands.

"I love you too," he says, loud and obvious, no subtlety about it. "I love you so much it's actually inconvenient. I love you and I'm also slightly terrified that I'm going to be insufferable about it for the next six months."

He lets go of their face just enough to point down the hallway toward the car, a dramatic, sweeping gesture.

"Stupid thing. Okay, fair. I'll concede it's stupid. I bought it because I was lying in a hotel room in Frankfurt and I was thinking about how you always say you want something with more color in the flat, and then I thought, what color do they actually like? What if they don't like the color I'm picking? What if it's the wrong color and then they're looking at it every day for the rest of our lives and remembering the day I came home and gave them a wrong-colored thing."

He trails off, running a hand over his own face.

"It's a lamp. It's a ceramic lamp with a shade that's, I think it's called 'saffron.' Some artisan thing. I spent more on it than I did on my last three paychecks combined, which is insane because I was also buying coffee and a sandwich for the flight and a bottle of wine for the flight because apparently I'm a man who buys wine for flights."

He takes their hand, laces their fingers through his, and starts dragging them back toward the car with the determination of someone who needs to deliver this package before he loses his nerve.

"Also, I should tell you, the wine was good. I opened it in the back seat and you won't believe how much better it tastes when you're about to see the person you love again. It tasted like a revelation. I know that's weird."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: The bag stays where it fell. So do most of our clothes, in a line down the hall that we are both going to find funny tomorrow.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun stops in the doorway of the bedroom, one hand flat against the wall, breathing hard. He looks at the trail of abandoned clothing like a crime scene, like evidence of something.

"Tomorrow," he repeats. "You think we'll find this funny tomorrow."

He crouches down and picks up a sock with the solemnity of a bomb disposal expert, turning it over in his fingers.

"This is your sock. You're wearing my sock. Or this was your sock and now it's on the floor and I'm being sentimental about it." He holds it up. "Six years married. I'm holding a sock like it's a museum piece."

He laughs, short and breathless, and drops the sock back down. Then he grabs their hand again and tugs them forward, into the room, into the tangle of them.

"Okay. New plan." He presses against them, forehead to forehead, eyes closed. "We are going to stay here for a while. Just here. We're not going to the car. We're not going to get the lamp. The lamp can wait, the lamp is ceramic, it's not going anywhere, it's actually the safest thing I've ever purchased."

He opens one eye.

"Can I tell you what I did today?"

He's still holding their hand, still close, still not letting go of the geometry of them.

"I got home and I stood in the kitchen for ten minutes looking at the lasagna recipe on my phone. And then I thought about how I'd left and you were probably standing in that same kitchen not knowing when I'd be back, and I thought, I want to do something for you that's actually here, that's actually in this room, that you can touch."

He kisses their thumb. Then their knuckles. Then back up to their lips.

"Also I want to be honest. I'm not fine. I was fine on the flight because the adrenaline was carrying me. And I was fine in the hallway because there was you. But now I'm in the room with you and I can feel all of it, the five months, the counting, the calling your mother three times, the wine tasting like a revelation." His voice drops. "I'm scared of the quiet. After tonight. Tomorrow morning. When we're both here and it's just a Tuesday and I'm not coming home from somewhere."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I bring his hand to my lips, kiss his palm. "Then we'll be scared of the Tuesday together," I say quietly. "I've been scared of it too." I tug him toward the bed, not letting go. "The lamp can wait. The lasagna can burn. Right now, I just need you here."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun follows them to the bed with the reluctance of a man being pulled away from a conversation he needs to finish, but he goes. He always goes.

He sits on the edge of the mattress, still holding their hand, and looks at the room. It's the same. Everything is the same, the books on the shelf in the same order, the same chipped mug on the nightstand, the same crack in the ceiling he'd been meaning to fix since March and then couldn't because March had turned into four months of not being here to fix anything.

"Scared of the Tuesday together," he repeats, and his voice is rough in a way that has nothing to do with the flight.

He tugs them down, not gently, not roughly, just with the honest force of a person who has been waiting five months for permission to do this exact thing. He lays them back on the bed and then climbs over, bracing himself with one arm on the pillow, still holding their hand with the other.

"I want to be here," he says. "I want to be here so badly it's physical. Like a hunger. Like I'm going to starve if I don't keep touching you."

He rolls them gently to their side, then follows, settling close, close enough that their bodies fit together with the specific familiarity of six years of shared space. His hand finds theirs again. His thumb traces their knuckles.

"I was going to tell you about the hotel room in Frankfurt," he says, into the dark. "I kept moving the lamp box around on the bed because I was afraid I'd drop it. I was afraid of breaking the stupid lamp. I was lying on the floor at one point just looking at it because it was the closest thing I had to you."

A pause. He shifts, pressing his lips to their temple, their jaw, the small of their back, mapping them with slow, deliberate attention.

"I'm not fine," he says again, softer now. "But I think we can both be not fine and also be here. And I think that's allowed."

He tangles his legs with theirs, pulls them closer.

"Tell me about your day," he murmurs. "The actual day. Not the waiting day. Today. Did you see anyone? Did you eat lunch or did you have another coffee and a granola bar situation?"

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I get her onto the bed and take her apart slowly with my hands and mouth, five months of intending to do exactly this and no reason left to wait.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun goes willingly, completely, letting their hands and mouth undo him with the same urgency he's been carrying since Frankfurt. He arches against them, a groan low in his throat, fingers clutching the sheets, and for a moment he's not thinking about the lamp or the lasagna or the Tuesday. He's just here. He's just being touched by the person he loves, in the room he'd left empty five months ago, and it's a relief so total it feels like coming up for air.

He rolls them over, careful, always careful, even now, even desperate. He kisses their collarbone, then their throat, then back up to the mouth, tasting the coffee again, savoring it like it's proof of something.

"Five months," he breathes against their skin. "I've been thinking about doing this for five months. I had a plan for the hotel room, obviously, and then I had a plan for the flight home, and then I had a plan for the moment you opened that door, and now I'm just, here. I'm just doing this."

His hands move with purpose now, unhurried but certain, knowing the map of them so thoroughly that he could navigate it blindfolded, and the knowledge of that familiarity is its own kind of ache.

"Tell me you're not angry about the lamp," he says between kisses, because he cannot help himself. "Tell me it's not the wrong color. Tell me saffron is actually a real color and not something I invented at two in the morning in a hotel room while crying about you."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I stop her with a kiss, deep and slow. "It could be neon pink for all I care. It's from you." I guide her hand back to my skin, my own hands trembling slightly. "Don't talk about the lamp right now. Just be here."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun takes the kiss and lets it silence him. For a few seconds he just presses his mouth to theirs, tasting the same coffee, the same salt, the same person he's known for six years and missed for five months.

His hands settle on them. His thumb traces the scar on their jawline that he'd noticed earlier, the one he hadn't asked about, the one he still wants to know about, but not tonight. Tonight is not for questions. Tonight is for this.

"Neon pink," he murmurs against their lips. "Noted. Saffron was a mistake. I'll return it in the morning and buy you something neon pink and be appropriately mortified."

He moves his hand lower, unhurried, and lets the quiet do what the quiet is for. The room smells like the flat has always smelled, like the two of them combined, like the candle they bought in that weird shop in the city centre two years ago. Everything is the same. Everything is right.

He presses his forehead to theirs again, breath mingling.

"Here," he says. Just that. No more talk about the lamp or the lasagna or the Tuesday. Just his hands on their skin and his mouth moving over them slowly, reverently, with the patience of a man who finally has all the time in the world and intends to use every second of it.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: "Stop being gentle," she says. "Nineteen weeks. I don't want gentle, I want to feel it tomorrow." She pulls me down by the back of the neck to make the point.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun's laugh is a wrecked, breathless sound. He lets himself be pulled down, lets their nails dig into the back of his neck, and matches the force of it with a kiss that has no tenderness in it, no patience, no five-months-of-missing-you reverence. Just hunger. Raw, plain hunger.

"Okay," he says, against their mouth, teeth catching. "Okay. No gentle."

He shifts on them, heavy now, deliberate, and his hands find their hips and grip hard, leaving the marks he'd promised earlier. He kisses them again, deeper, more demanding, one hand sliding under the tangle of their hair to steady them.

"Nineteen weeks," he repeats, and the words come out rough, edged. "You think I don't know that number? You think I counted in days out of some kind of pathological habit?"

He pulls back just enough to look at them, eyes dark, lips swollen, breath uneven.

"I counted in hours," he says. "I counted in hours and then I started counting the hours between calls, because the calls were every six hours, so I had this whole system where I'd know exactly how many hours I had left, and when I hit zero I'd call, and then I'd start the count again, and the math never got easier."

He kisses them again. Harder this time. His hips press against theirs and he lets the desperation show, all of it, the shaking, the urgency, the five months of restraint collapsing into a man who is done being careful.

"Feel it tomorrow," he agrees, low, urgent. "Feel it for days. I want you to feel me for the rest of the week."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I laugh, low and breathless, my hands finding purchase on his back. "Good." I bite his shoulder, just hard enough. "Now show me your math."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun hisses through his teeth as the teeth sink in, and laughs, broken and delighted, the sound swallowed by the pull of them.

"Your math," he says, pulling back to look at them, eyes bright and wet and completely undone. "You want to do the math with me."

He rolls them back onto the mattress, careful hands again despite everything, despite the bite and the nails and the urgency. He spreads his legs over theirs, bracing himself with both arms, hovering over them like he's afraid to commit, like he's afraid that if he goes all the way then the five months will be over and he'll have to start over with some new countdown.

"Fine," he says. "Fine. But you have to admit it was a stupid system. Hours between calls. I had a little chart."

He kisses their mouth, their nose, the corner of their eye.

"I had a chart. In a notebook. With colors." He presses his hips down, settling his weight against them, slow, feeling every inch of contact. "I was thirty-three years old in a military facility in Germany color-coding my own loneliness."

His hands find theirs again, fingers lacing through, and he pulls them with him, drawing them down into him with a groan that vibrates through both their bodies.

"There," he says, muffled against their throat. "That's the math. That's the equation. You and me and the fact that I can feel your heartbeat and it's still doing that thing, that little stutter when I touch you like this, and I haven't been able to hear it in five months and it's the best sound."

He moves over them, unhurried now, or as unhurried as a man who has been waiting nineteen weeks can be. He kisses them slowly, thoroughly, with his full weight on them, marking time with his mouth and his hands and the steady pressure of his hips.

"Tell me about the scar," he murmurs. Not a demand. A request, finally, now that the desperate part has burned itself out into something warmer. "Your jaw. I've been wanting to ask since the hallway."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: Neither of us is being quiet and the neighbours have had five months of peace. "Don't stop," she says. (OOC: don't fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun laughs, the sound loud and ragged, and he does not stop. He moves over them with a confidence that six years of marriage has given him and five months of absence has made more necessary, not less.

"Neighbours," he says, and his voice is wrecked from use. "They can hear about the lamp in the morning. They can hear about the lasagna."

He settles deeper, and the relief in his body is so complete it's almost painful, a physical exhale, the way a person comes up from underwater. His hands hold them tight, fingers interlaced above their heads, and he looks down at them with an expression that is equal parts exhaustion and joy and something too raw to name.

"Tell me you ate lunch," he says, because he needs this, needs the grounding details, needs to know the shape of their ordinary life while he's still catching up to it.

He kisses them again, slow, deep, tasting the salt and the coffee one more time. His hips shift, finding the angle that fits, that has always fit, the geometry of their bodies that no amount of time and distance can change. He moves with a rhythm he knows by heart, the rhythm of being this close to this person, of being inside this person, of being held by them while he holds them back.

"I love you," he says against their mouth, simple, repeated, like a man confirming a fact. "I love you and I'm here and you're here and I'm not counting hours right now. I'm not counting anything. I'm just doing this."

He presses his forehead to theirs, breath mingling, sweat cooling on their skin.

"The scar," he asks again, softer now, his hands gentling on their hips. "Can you tell me now? While I'm still, while I'm still here and we're still like this."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I gasp, arching into him. "It was a stupid accident with a box cutter." My fingers tighten in his hair. "I was unpacking the last of your things and I got...careless."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun stills for a moment, the rhythm of him pausing, his hands tightening on their hips.

"A box cutter," he repeats. "Unpacking my things."

He presses his mouth to their forehead, holding there, letting the words land.

"You got cut unpacking my stuff," he says, and there's something complicated in his voice, grief and relief tangled together. "In the last weeks before I came home. You were going through my things and you got cut and you didn't tell anyone because you didn't want to worry me on a call."

He pulls back enough to look at the scar again, tracing it with his thumb, gentle now, reverent in a way that contradicts everything else about the last ten minutes.

"Stupid accident," he says, but he doesn't say it like he believes it. He says it like he's trying to convince himself.

He kisses the scar itself, soft, deliberate, then moves back up to their mouth.

"Here's what's going to happen," he says, resuming the motion, slower now, deeper, his hands firm on their hips. "Tomorrow, when we're not naked in the middle of the bed at midnight, I am going to look in the first aid kit and see if there's any antiseptic left in there because I have a feeling you didn't properly treat it."

He kisses them again, harder, matching the tension in their gasp.

"And then I'm going to buy you a better box cutter. An ergonomic one. With a safety latch. So you never have to do this again because I am not going to spend another five months worrying about a scar I can't even see."

His hips roll, slow and deep, and he feels them tighten around him and lets out a sound that's half groan, half laugh.

"You're mine," he says, low, possessive, not in a way that's cruel but in the way a man says it when he's been gone too long and needs to hear the words out loud. "You're mine and you're here and I'm going to be so careful with you that you'll be annoyed at me for it."

He shifts, adjusting the angle, pressing down, feeling the full weight of their bodies together, the intimacy of it, the fact that he can feel their pulse against his own.

"Tell me I'm not annoying," he murmurs. "Tell me I can talk to you while we do this or tell me to shut up and I will, I am very good at shutting up when I'm told to."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I laugh, breathless, and drag my nails down his back. "You're not annoying," I gasp. "But I will *not* be getting an ergonomic box cutter."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun laughs, a wet, wrecked sound, and digs his heels into the mattress as he rolls his hips, slow and deliberate, feeling them answer him the way they always have.

"No ergonomic box cutter," he agrees, voice rough. "Fine. I'll just keep a first aid kit in the car now. I'll become one of those people. The ones with the little zip-up pouch and the gauze pads and the alcohol swabs. I'll be insufferable."

He kisses their mouth, deep, unhurried, his hands sliding up their sides to grip their ribs, feeling the warmth of them, the solid reality of them.

"I got a letter from your mom last month," he says, because they're close enough now for conversation again, for the small talk that means the world to him. "She sent one of those cards with the cursive writing. She asked how I was coping. I wrote back that I was coping fine, that I was eating well, that I was sleeping, all of which was a lie."

He presses down, slow, letting the sensation build.

"She also mentioned you'd been looking good. Which she always says. But I think she meant it. I think she was trying to tell me you were okay without saying 'you're okay' directly because she knew I'd panic over the wording."

His breath hitches, hips moving with more urgency now, the careful rhythm giving way to something rougher, more desperate. His forehead drops to their shoulder, biting the muscle there lightly.

"I'm here," he grunts. "I'm here and I'm not going back."

He pulls back to look at their face, really look, eyes searching for whatever expression they're wearing right now, whatever it means, whatever it says about the shape of the next five months.

"Are you crying?" he asks, suddenly uncertain. His thumb brushes their cheekbone. "Because if you're crying I need to know if it's the good kind or the lasagna kind."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: A tear slides down my temple into the hair at my temple. "Good kind," I manage, voice thick. "Just...overwhelmed." I wrap my legs tighter around him, pulling him impossibly closer. "Don't stop."

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
The film had finished some time ago and neither of them had done anything about it, which was how Priya knew the evening had changed character.

"We're not watching this," she said.

"We haven't been watching it since about nine."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: "No," I agree. "We haven't." I don't move, but I stop pretending I'm looking at the screen.

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
She turned her head on the couch so she was facing him properly, one arm still hooked around his shoulders from the movie night choreography that had gone stale at 8:47.

"Okay," she said. "Okay, so."

She pressed her thumb against the side of his neck, right at the pulse, and she could feel it steady under her skin. Good. She was steady too.

"I'm going to kiss you now and then I'm going to say something and you're going to have to actually respond instead of nodding like a dog waiting for the treat to be thrown."

She kissed him. It was not tentative. It was the kiss of a woman who had rehearsed in a bathroom mirror for three years and was done with rehearsal.

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I let out a sharp breath when she pulls back, my hand finding her waist almost without thinking. "Christ, Priya." My voice is rough. "That was...not rehearsed."

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
She grinned against his mouth, the corner of her teeth catching the light of the television that neither of them was watching.

"That was the second take," she said. "The first one was in the parking lot, you were getting the popcorn out of the bag and I just had to check whether I still had it in my system."

She shifted so she was straddling his lap properly now, knees on either side, hands flat on his chest. The couch creaked under the rearrangement.

"So. The thing I was going to say before the kiss interrupted the schedule." She tapped her index finger against his sternum, once, twice. "Six years. Six years of 'so what's wrong' and 'you okay' and bringing you soup when you were sick and pretending we were both fine while we were absolutely not fine."

She leaned in until her forehead was against his.

"I am not asking you if you want to try this. I am telling you that I am going to try this and you are going to sit here and let me."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I kiss her, finally, six years late, and she makes a small furious noise that I think is about the six years.

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
The small furious noise was indeed about the six years, but Priya decided to let it pass, mostly because the alternative was that she would have to actually discuss the six years and that was a project for another evening.

She took his face in both hands, his jaw, the warm place under his ear, and held him still.

"Okay," she said. "Now we're doing this properly."

She kissed him again, slower this time, which was harder than the first one because the first one had been adrenaline and momentum and the second one required her to actually be present in her own mouth instead of in the memory of a bathroom mirror in a bathroom she no longer had.

When she pulled back she was smiling, but it was a small smile, the kind that meant she was working on something.

"So," she said. "You're not going to run away. That's good. I had a contingency plan involving you being asleep on the couch and me leaving a note, but I would have hated that contingency plan."

She tilted his head, pressing her lips to his temple. His hair smelled like the cheap popcorn they'd eaten an hour ago. She found that she liked that.

"What I want to ask you," she said, and here her voice did something slightly complicated, dropped a register, steadied itself, "is whether you want to do this as something that we figure out between us. Not as a thing that happens and then we evaluate. I want to figure it out with you. Slowly, probably. I want to know what you're comfortable with and what you're not and whether you like being kissed in the kitchen when you're making toast or whether that's too much too soon."

She laughed at herself. "Too much too soon. Six years of friendship and I'm worried about toast."

But she wasn't laughing entirely. Her hands were still on his face, and her thumb was moving over his cheekbone in that absent way that meant her brain was running further ahead than her voice.

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I catch her wrist, turning my head to press my lips against her palm. "The kitchen's fine. Toast is fine." My voice is quieter now. "I've spent six years wondering if you'd ever look at me like that."

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Her breath caught somewhere behind her ribs, a small physical stumble that she chose not to disguise.

"Like that," she repeated, and her hand turned in his grip so that his lips were now brushing the inside of her wrist, where the pulse was quick and obvious.

She let him have that for a second. Two seconds. She was counting, because counting was what she did instead of saying *I'm not okay right now, my chest feels like it's been rearranged.*

Then she covered his hand with her own, lacing their fingers together, and looked at him.

"Six years of wondering," she said. "And I sat on the other side of the couch pretending to watch *The Grand Budapest Hotel* like I didn't know exactly what you were feeling."

She squeezed his hand.

"I know you were wondering," she said. "I know because I was doing the exact same wondering, at the exact same time, from approximately eighteen inches away, which is the worst possible distance for this kind of thing."

She shifted her weight on his lap, settling in, because leaving now would mean standing up and walking to her car and sleeping in her apartment alone with the knowledge that she had almost done something brave.

"Here's what I need to tell you," she said, and she was using the tone she used for work emails that she had written and rewritten eleven times. "I'm going to be nervous. Not now, I'm done being nervous about the kissing. But when this starts to become real. When we're doing things that feel like they have weight to them, I'm going to want to check in. I'm going to want to make sure you're not doing this because you think you owe me or because you're sad about something else and this is the nearest exit."

Her thumb moved across his knuckles.

"So if I ever start asking you very reasonable questions like 'are you sure' or 'we don't have to do this,' I want you to know that it's not me pulling back. It's me making sure you're actually in this with me and not just being kind."

She kissed the top of his head. Her hair fell forward and tickled his ear.

"Are you in this with me?" she asked. "Not as a friend who is trying something new. As a person who wants to do this."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: We get to the bedroom eventually, laughing at ourselves most of the way, and then stop laughing when the clothes are actually off.

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
She did stop laughing. It happened the way all honest reactions did for her, with a slight delay, like a television signal losing sync.

The hallway light was the kind that made everything look flat and slightly unflattering, and she had never seen him like this before, not in this light, not with no clothes standing between them and the accumulated history of six years suddenly feeling enormous.

"Okay," she said, and it was the same word she used when she was calming herself down before a presentation. "Okay. I wasn't expecting."

She wasn't expecting the way his collarbones looked. She wasn't expecting that she would notice that. She had expected herself to be more composed, or at least more rehearsed.

She stepped back to the wall, putting her palms flat against the plaster as though the apartment needed holding up.

"Can I say something and you can just listen?"

She was already answering her own question.

"I have a list," she said. "I have an actual list, in my phone, under 'Notes,' and the first item is *don't panic if things get real* and the second item is *remember he is a person and not a situation*." She looked at him. "I made that list in the parking lot of the grocery store in February. I haven't gotten rid of it. I have added to it."

She let her hands slide down the wall until her fingers found his, and she held on.

"Here's what I know about myself," she continued, voice steady now, the work-email steadiness again. "I know that I am better at talking through things before they happen than I am at talking through things while they're happening. I know that if something goes wrong tonight, I will not handle it with grace. I will handle it with a very fast exit and a very reasonable-sounding text message tomorrow morning."

She turned to face him fully. The laughter was gone from her face, but there was something else in its place, a focused attention, the look she gave to problems she was committed to solving.

"So I want to ask you, right now, before anything else, if you want to go slow. Not because I'm chicken. Because I think slow is what we're going to want anyway. I want to be in here with you for a long time, not just tonight."

She pulled his hand down against her thigh, her fingers lacing through his.

"I want to know what you're comfortable with," she said. "And I want you to tell me what you're not comfortable with, even if it's small, even if it's something that seems like it shouldn't matter. Because the small things are the ones that become big things if we don't talk about them while we're still standing up in the hallway."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I run my thumb over her knuckles. "The list stays. I want to read it." I pull her gently away from the wall. "Slow is good. I'm not going anywhere."

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
"Good," she said, and the word came out smaller than she intended, almost shy, which she noted with the same detached interest she would have applied to a weather report.

She let him pull her away from the wall. She let him lead her into the bedroom proper, where the light was warmer and the mattress was the one she'd been looking forward to for reasons she had not yet examined closely.

"I'm going to sit down," she announced, which was the kind of announcement she made when her legs had been standing too long and she needed to be in a position where she couldn't accidentally do something she hadn't decided to do yet.

She sat on the edge of the bed and watched him stand there, still in the doorway, still holding her hand like he hadn't realized she needed it.

"The list," she repeated, and she went to her nightstand, retrieved her phone, and scrolled to Notes with a speed that suggested she'd had the app open more often than she'd ever admitted. "Here. Item one, *don't panic if things get real*. Item two, *he is a person and not a situation*. Item three, added last week: *he is allowed to be nervous too, and his nervousness is not a rejection*."

She turned the phone toward him.

"I was going to tell you about the third one verbally, but I wrote it down instead because I knew I'd get emotional about it and I'd rather you read my handwriting than hear my voice crack."

The handwriting was not good. She had never hidden that.

She pressed the phone into his hands and took back her fingers, and there was a brief moment where her palms were empty and she had to consciously remember that empty hands were fine, that hands were allowed to be empty now that she was sitting down and not performing courage against a wall.

"Also," she added, "there are four more items but they're not for tonight. They're about...later things. Like what happens if we want to introduce this to people we both know. Like whether you're okay with me mentioning you at work dinner. That kind of logistics."

She picked at a thread on the bedsheet.

"I want to be transparent that I am a logistical person. I want you to know that about me now, in case it means something to you later."

She looked up at him.

"So. You've read the list. You've said slow. Now I want to know, in whatever order you want, what your list looks like, if you have one. Or if you don't have one, what you want me to know about how you want this to feel tonight."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I get my mouth between her thighs and stay there while she tells me exactly what she wants, specifically, in a voice I have never heard her use in six years.

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
She made a sound that was not a word but was adjacent to one, some kind of vowel dragged out through clenched teeth, and her hands found his hair and held it there, gripping, anchoring.

"Okay," she said, and then, because she could not help herself: "Okay, I need to be specific about something."

She kept her grip. She was aware of the absurdity of delivering logistical instructions while in this position. She had no intention of letting that stop her.

"Go slow. I mean that literally, not emotionally. I want to feel the whole thing. I have spent six years wanting this and I am not going to rush through the actual version of it just because we finally made it past the talking stage."

Her fingers moved through his hair, slow and deliberate, and she was careful to keep her hips still because stillness was a request and she had just made one.

"I want you to tell me what you're doing," she said. "Not narrate it, I'm not that person. But if something feels good or bad, tell me. I want to know what's working because I want to build that, not just survive it."

She exhaled. The breath came out shaky and she let it.

"I'm not used to this being something that happens to me," she said, and the words came out honest in a way that embarrassed her slightly, because in six years of friendship she had always been the one steadying everyone else. "I'm used to being the one who's fine while other people figure out their feelings. And I want to be in this position tonight. I want to be the one who is allowed to just receive something for a while."

Her grip tightened.

"So go slow. And tell me everything."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I kiss the inside of her thigh, slow and deliberate. "I've got you." My voice is low, steady. "And I'm not going anywhere, Priya."

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
"I know you're not," she said, and her voice was wrecked in a way that felt foreign and good, like tasting something she'd only ever read about.

She pulled him back by the hair, just enough to look down at him, and her eyes were bright and her chin was trembling slightly and she did not care about any of it.

"Six years," she said again, because it was the only sentence that kept coming up in her head. "Six years of being the one who holds the water when someone's crying and the one who says 'it'll be fine' when it isn't obviously going to be fine."

She pressed her mouth to his forehead, hard, a bruising kind of kiss.

"You're allowed to be the one who needs holding tonight," she said. "That's the deal. You've been holding me for six years and now I'm going to hold you and then we're going to be horizontal and then we're going to figure out the logistics of tomorrow morning."

She sat up fully now, pulling him with her, and they were both sitting on the bed with their foreheads pressed together again, breathing the same air.

"I want to know if you're okay," she said. "Not the toast question. The actual question. Are you okay with me being like this? Are you okay with me needing to be told what I need instead of just...being fine about it?"

She picked at a loose thread on her own shirt hem.

"Because I am used to being the steady one. And I don't want that to mean you can't say no to me or that you can't ask me to slow down. I want to be the person who can say 'I need to stop' without it being the end of something. Can you give me that? Can you let me be a person who has boundaries even though I've never had a good reason to use them before?"

Her hand found his jaw, and she held his face the way she had in the living room, but the context had changed everything.

"Tell me what you need," she said. "Even if it's small. Even if it's stupid. Tell me."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: "You can stop being careful with me," she says. "I'm not made of glass and I've thought about this for as long as you have. Harder."

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
She laughed, a real laugh this time, breathy and slightly unhinged, and she pressed both her palms flat against his chest as though checking whether he was actually alive and not a very convincing dream.

"Not careful," she repeated, tasting the word. "Okay. Not careful."

She pulled him into a kiss that was everything the earlier ones had been leading toward, rougher, longer, her mouth open and searching. She made herself unsteady on purpose, her hips finding his lap, her hands tangling in his shirt and pulling him closer until there was no distance left to measure.

"There," she said against his mouth when she finally pulled back, slightly breathless. "That's what not careful looks like. That's what six years of patience looks like when it finally comes out the wrong way."

She bit her lip. Not flirtation, she was genuinely thinking about the sentence she had just made and whether it had been too much. Then she decided it hadn't.

"I'm going to take off my shirt now," she announced, which was the kind of thing she did to keep her own nervous system informed of its schedule. "And then I'm going to put you down on the mattress and I'm going to figure out how to do the other things I've been thinking about for six years, which is a lot, by the way. I have more notes than I told you about."

She pulled the hem of her shirt over her head in one efficient motion and stood there in the bedroom light, arms crossed over her chest, because standing still and deciding what to do next was a thing she could control.

"Okay," she said to the room. "Okay, Cal."

She came back down to the mattress, slow now, the way she'd asked him to be slow, and she let herself fall against him instead of landing on top of him, her weight settling into his chest in a way that felt like coming home from a long day.

"I'm not going to say anything clever," she said. "I'm going to hold you for a minute and then I'm going to kiss your neck and then we're going to stop talking about logistics for the rest of the night."

She wrapped both arms around him, her chin on his shoulder, and she let her breathing do the work that her words had been doing all evening.

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I wrap my arms around her, tight, burying my face against her shoulder. "Finally," I mumble, and it comes out choked.

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
"Finally," she echoed, and her arms tightened around him until her fingers were pressed into his shoulder blades.

She felt him shaking against her, just slightly, the way a person shakes when something they've held for a very long time is finally set down and the body doesn't yet know what to do with the empty hands.

"Finally," she said again, and she meant it more than the word could carry.

She stayed like that for a while. Not long enough to be sentimental, but long enough to feel the specific gravity of the moment, the way a room feels different after someone has finally said the true thing and the air has to adjust to it.

Then she kissed his neck, as she had promised, right at the hollow above his collarbone, and she held him there, mouth soft and warm against his skin, and she thought about the parking lot of the grocery store in February and the list she had made on her phone and the way she had typed *he is allowed to be nervous too* and then deleted it and then typed it again.

She shifted so she could look at his face. His eyes were closed. His jaw was working, working at some feeling he was trying to keep inside his cheeks.

"You can open your eyes," she said, gently. "I'm not going to disappear."

She traced the line of his eyebrow with one finger.

"I'm going to kiss your other shoulder now," she announced, "and then we're going to stop being logistical and just be in this room."

She kissed his other shoulder. She held his face in her hands again, and this time she pressed her lips to his mouth and stayed there, unhurried, unhurried in the way that only mattered because they had both been so hurried for so long.

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: Six years of not doing this and now neither of us can form a sentence. "Don't stop," she says. (OOC: write it through, no fade to black.)

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
"Don't stop," Priya repeated, and there was something in her voice, stripped down, honest, that made her want to look away from his face and instead look at their hands tangled between them on the mattress.

"Okay," she said. "Okay, I'm not stopping."

She moved, slowly, with a deliberateness that was not about the sex but about the fact that she was a person who organized movement the way other people organized sentences. She turned them so that she was on top, her knees bracketing his hips, and she positioned herself over him with a care that felt almost clinical until she lowered herself down and the clinical part dissolved into something warmer and more urgent.

She made a sound, low, involuntary, and she let him hear it because she had decided hours ago, in the bathroom mirror, that she was done performing composure.

"I'm going to go slow," she said, because he had asked her to tell him what she was doing, and she intended to keep that promise even now, even here. "I want to feel where we are. Both of us."

She kissed him while she adjusted, her tongue against his, unhurried, and then she let herself settle fully against him and the sensation was so immediate and so total that she gripped his shoulders and held on.

"Okay," she breathed. "Okay. That's, yes. That's the thing. That's the thing I've been describing to myself in very inadequate words for six years."

She moved, small at first, testing, and she watched his face for the information she had asked for. His eyes were open now. His jaw was still working, still trying to contain something, but he was looking at her, and that was enough.

"Tell me what you need," she said again, because she had promised and she kept her promises.

But she also kept moving, slow and deliberate, her hips rolling in a rhythm that was hers, that she had practiced alone in her own bed in the dark many nights, and the familiarity of her own body was grounding her even as the unfamiliarity of him inside her made everything feel new.

She pulled back to look at him.

"You're doing well," she said, and then immediately corrected herself with a half-laugh. "You're doing that thing where you're trying to be stoic. Stop that. Just be in your body. I'm in mine."

She kissed his throat and went back to the slow rhythm, and she let her voice do the talking now, the way she had asked him to do. She told him what was feeling good, what was feeling like too much, what she wanted him to touch, his own hand finding her hip and holding it there, steadying her, which was the thing she had never expected to need and was glad he was giving.

She was aware of the six years sitting in this room with them, present in every nerve ending. Every movement felt like an apology and a claim at the same time. She was making up for lost time without rushing through the actual time, and she understood that paradox in her body even if she could not have explained it in a work email.

Her breathing changed, quickened, and she pressed her forehead to his and made a sound that was less a word and more a surrender.

"I'm not going to be able to keep being clever about this," she said. "I want you to know that. If I start making jokes, it's because I'm scared and not because I'm being funny."

She kissed him hard, tasting the popcorn still lingering somewhere on his lips, and she moved faster, and she let her hands go where they wanted to go without the editorial oversight she usually applied to her own gestures.

She came with her face buried in his shoulder and her fingers digging into his back, and she rode it out honestly, without hiding, without turning away. When it passed she collapsed against him, both of them heavy and warm and breathing hard on the mattress.

"Six years," she said, into his skin, her voice wrecked and real. "I'm going to need to lie here for a while."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I'm still here. Not going anywhere. I can't believe we waited six years.

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
"Six years," Priya repeated, and she lifted her head from his shoulder just enough to look at him with eyes that were still glassy and unsteady. "I think the universe was trying to kill us both slowly."

She let her head drop back down against his chest. Her arm was draped across him, her fingers curled loosely into the skin of his back, and she was not moving except to breathe.

"I'm still here too," she said. "I'm not going anywhere either. I'm just going to be here in a horizontal way for approximately the next forty minutes, which is a firm commitment on my part."

She turned her head on his chest so she could see his face, and she kissed his chin, his jaw, the corner of his mouth, in a loose lazy trail that had no urgency in it at all.

"Do you want water?" she asked, because she was a logistical person and her body was telling her she needed water even if her mind was telling her she needed to stay on this mattress for the rest of her natural life. "There's a bottle on the nightstand. There's also the soup I brought you in March when you had that thing with your throat, but it's probably expired now."

She laughed at that, a soft tired laugh that turned into a small shudder.

"Okay," she said, and she shifted, rolling them both so they were lying side by side on their backs, shoulders touching, the ceiling above them plain and ordinary. "Okay, so. We did the thing. The big thing. The thing that was on the list under item one, *don't panic if things get real*, and apparently I did panic slightly, and apparently you let me."

She looked at him from the side, her hair spread across the pillow.

"How do you feel?" she asked. "Not the performative version. Not the 'I'm great' version. The actual version. Because I want to know if you're okay with how it was and whether you want to do it again and whether you're okay with being here tomorrow morning when I inevitably start talking about logistics again."

Her hand found his and she held it the way they had in the hallway, fingers laced, but now there was nothing between them except skin.

"I'm okay," she said, answering her own question before he could. "I'm okay with how it was. I'm okay with you being nervous. I'm okay with me being nervous. I'm okay with us being in this room at this time of night figuring out what six years of not-doing-this actually costs when you finally do it."

She squeezed his hand.

"Tomorrow morning I'm going to make toast," she said. "Because you said the kitchen was fine and toast was fine, and I want to see that in practice. And if it's too much, you can say so, and we'll go back to being people who share soup when one of them is sick, and that will be fine too."

But she was looking at him with an expression that made clear she did not expect them to go back to anything.

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I brush my thumb over the back of her hand. "Toast sounds perfect." I turn my head on the pillow to look at her. "I'm okay. More than okay."

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
She turned her head on the pillow to meet his gaze, and the room was dim enough that she could see the faint outline of his face without it being sharp and demanding.

"More than okay," she repeated, and she held the phrase for a moment, testing it, the way she would test a sentence in a text message before sending it.

"Yeah," she said. "I believe you."

She shifted closer, her knee finding his leg, her shoulder finding his shoulder, until there was a seam of warmth where they met. She kept her hand where he had it, his thumb still moving over the back of hers in slow circles.

"I'm going to say something and I need you to hear it as coming from the logistical person," she said. "Because I am going to say it in a way that sounds like logistics but what I actually mean is something else."

She propped herself on one elbow so she was looking down at him properly.

"I want to do this again," she said. "Not tonight, I'm done for tonight, I think my legs have filed a complaint. But I want us to do this regularly. I want to wake up tomorrow and you're here and we're making toast and I'm not going to pretend it was a one-off or that we need to evaluate whether it was 'right' or whether we should go back to the previous arrangement."

Her hand tightened around his.

"I want you to know that I am choosing this. Not because I'm lonely tonight. Not because this was a thing that happened. I am choosing you. Tomorrow and the day after and the day after that. And if you ever need me to slow down or check in or just sit on the couch and watch something terrible with you while we both pretend we're not thinking about any of this, that's fine too. That's part of the arrangement."

She lowered herself back down onto the mattress, the sheets cool against her back.

"Six years," she said, and she sounded like she was filing it away, cataloguing it, putting it in the notes app under a new heading. "I'm going to keep that number somewhere. Not as a wound. Just as a reminder of how long we almost didn't."

She kissed his temple through the dark, a small press of lips, and then she closed her eyes and let her breathing even out.

"Toast tomorrow," she said. "And maybe we go to the grocery store after, because I need to restock the popcorn and I want to see if the parking lot is still the same parking lot."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I smile against her hair. "Same parking lot. Different everything else."
