dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The party had reached the stage where nobody would notice two people missing, which Odile pointed out approximately four seconds before doing something about it.

"The bathroom upstairs has a lock," she said, into Fen's ear, over the music.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Does it work?" I ask, already moving toward the stairs.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
"It worked when I tested it earlier," Odile lied smoothly, grabbing his wrist and steering him up the carpeted staircase. The bass thumped through the floorboards with each step, a steady rhythm that she decided was useful. Useful for covering sounds, useful for keeping her own pulse from being an obvious thing.

She pushed through the bathroom door first, shoulder-checking the frame, then turned to lock it behind them. The click of the latch was tiny and loud and probably inaudible over the party, but she flinched anyway, pressing her back against the sink.

"So." She exhaled through her nose, looking at the mirror above them. Her reflection stared back, flushed cheeks, wineglass abandoned somewhere downstairs, a smear of lipstick on her collarbone. "You're sure about this. In my friend's house."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I grin, leaning against the door. "I'm sure about you. The house is just a bonus." I reach out and trace the lipstick smear with my thumb. "Though I think you missed a spot."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile made a sound that was half laugh, half protest, swatting his hand away before it could do anything else.

"The lipstick is not a spot," she said, though she was already reaching for her collarbone, smearing the mark further across her skin rather than cleaning it. Better that way. Evidence of the night, scattered about. "And you're not leaning against the door like you're guarding it. The lock is on the inside. You're just being dramatic."

She crossed the small bathroom in two steps, pulling the curtain around the tub for what was probably no privacy benefit whatsoever. The water running from the showerhead was a nice detail, though. Someone had left it on. She turned it up to full blast, steam immediately curling up from the porcelain rim.

"Okay," she said, settling onto the edge of the tub, legs swinging. "Now you can say whatever it is you wanted to say. Because you've been looking at me for twenty minutes with that expression, and I know that expression. You're about to be either very sweet or very stupid."

She picked at a hangnail on her thumb, studying the grout lines in the wall as though they were fascinating.

Fen:
"Both, actually." I step closer, catching her wrist gently. "You've been dancing like you wanted to be grabbed for an hour. I figured I'd wait until there was a door that locked."

Odile:

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I get the door shut and her against it, and downstairs somebody turns the music up, which helps.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile let out a short, breathless laugh against the door, her hip knocking his as she pressed flat against the wood. The lock turned again, just to be safe. She did it with deliberate slowness, thumb and forefinger working the latch, eyes already on his mouth.

"An hour," she repeated. "You stood there for an hour while I danced with people I don't even like, just to be patient." She shook her head, smiling. "You're insufferable. I hate that I find it romantic."

Her free hand came up, fingers hooking into the fabric at his collar, and she pulled him in hard enough that her forehead landed against his. The shower steamed around them, fogging the mirror into a useless white smear.

"Here," she whispered, because the music downstairs had shifted into something with a lot of bass and very little melody, and because her voice was doing something unpredictable. "You wanted to grab me. Go ahead and grab me. I've been waiting."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I slide my hands down her sides and grip her hips, pinning her to the door. "I wasn't being patient," I say, my voice low against the sound of the shower. "I was waiting for you to look at me like you are right now."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's breath hitched, a small, involuntary thing, and she hated herself for how obvious it sounded in the enclosed steam.

"Look at me," she said back, as though he needed to be told. Her thumbs dug into the fabric at his hips, pulling him closer until there was no sensible distance left between them. "I've been looking at you since the parking lot. I just didn't want to do it where anyone could see."

She tilted her chin up, studying his face with an intensity that was almost aggressive, almost too direct. The steam blurred everything past the length of her arms, which she thought was rather poetic.

"You know what I keep thinking?" she murmured, her nose brushing his as she spoke. "That you're going to say something incredibly smooth right now. Something rehearsed. And I'm going to roll my eyes at you, and then I'm going to kiss you anyway, and we'll pretend the eye-rolling didn't happen."

She was already leaning in to start that kiss, slow and deliberate, tasting of the wine she'd abandoned downstairs. Her hands slid up his chest, fingers curling into his shirt, mapping the familiar lines there.

"And if you don't say anything," she continued, breaking the kiss only far enough to speak against his mouth, "that's fine too. I'll take silence. I'll take silence over most things you've said this year."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: There isn't room to do this properly and we don't let that stop us. Enough clothes come off to be a problem if anyone knocks.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile let out a startled little giggle, muffled against his mouth, because that was true and she had not considered the logistics.

"Right," she said, pulling back just enough to assess the situation. "Right. The door."

She shoved her phone into her cleavage rather than her back pocket, because back pocket was occupied by his hands, and then began the complicated business of undoing herself. Her own top came off quickly, pushed up and over her head with a speed that was entirely deliberate, because she wanted to see his face when he saw her. She kept her bra on, though. That felt like the appropriate level of commitment for a locked bathroom at someone else's party.

"Your shirt," she said, tugging at the hem of his. "It's too loud. It has a pattern. I don't like it."

She was already working at the buttons, her fingers fumbling in a way that made her groan in mild frustration. The steam was making everything slick and difficult. She grabbed a fistful of the fabric and yanked upward, exposing the warm skin of his stomach, and pressed her palm flat there for a moment, just feeling him.

"So," she said, looking up at him with a crooked grin. "What do we do now, in this little steaming closet, with enough clothes off that we look like a very committed couple doing something very improper?"

She pressed her body against his again, the door between her and the wall, her back to the cool wood.

"Because I want to say, for the record, that if anyone does knock, we are going to blame it on the humidity."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I laugh against her skin, my hands sliding up her back. "We're blaming the lipstick smear, actually." I kiss the spot she'd missed earlier. "And you're the one who turned the shower on. This was all your plan."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile bit her lower lip hard enough to leave a mark, because his hands on her back had gone from casual to somewhere else entirely and she needed to say something before she forgot how.

"The shower was an accident," she lied, breathless, pressing her back harder against the door. "I stumbled into it. It was a very dramatic stumble."

His kiss against her collarbone made her shoulders roll up toward her ears, a full-body reaction she had no control over and no shame in, honestly. She turned her head to look at him, hair plastered to her cheek with steam, eyes bright and a little unfocused.

"You know what's funny?" she said, her voice dropping to that low register she got when she was trying to be coy and failing. "I thought this would be the part where I was nervous. Where I'd be thinking about your parents knowing you, or your ex, or the fact that you've been sober and together for a while and this is just... us being normal in an abnormal way."

Her fingers found his waist again, dragging her nails lightly down the side of his ribs.

"Instead I'm thinking about whether the lipstick smear actually looks like a smudge or a deliberate smudge, and whether there's a difference."

She pulled him down into a kiss that was nothing like the first one, rougher, less careful, her mouth open against his with an eagerness she'd been holding back all night. When she broke away, she made a small, undignified sound.

"Okay," she said, laughing, pressing her forehead to his again. "That's better. That's much better."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I get my hand between her legs and she bites down on my shoulder to keep quiet, which works for about thirty seconds.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's teeth pressed hard against his shoulder, her whole body braced against the door behind her, and she was proud of herself for the thirty seconds. Genuinely proud.

Then she released his shoulder with a wet, embarrassed sound and grabbed his wrist instead, dragging his hand down to her hip where she could control the pace.

"Thirty seconds," she hissed, breathless, eyes wide. "That's a personal record. I'm going to put that in my little diary somewhere."

She laughed, a breathy, shaky thing, and pressed her mouth back to his shoulder to bite at it again, gentler this time, more playful. The steam was everywhere now, fogged the mirror completely, turned the bathroom into a warm, enclosed world where the only things that existed were the shower's roar, the thump of the bass through the ceiling, and the two of them pressed together against the lock.

"Okay," she said, pulling back to look at him with water beading on her shoulders. "Okay. I'm going to need you to be very quiet, because I'm about to make a very loud sound, and I need you to either cover my mouth or cover yours or do something useful with your other hand."

She shifted her weight, turning slightly so her back was fully against the door, giving him room to work. Her fingers tangled in his hair, holding him there, keeping his face level with hers even as her hips moved against his hand in a way she was not pretending was accidental.

"And Fen," she said, one eyebrow raised, a ghost of a smile on her mouth. "If you start narrating this like you're describing a painting, I will actually bite you. Not shoulder-level. Neck-level. You've been warned."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "I'm not an artist, I'm a mechanic," I mutter, my free hand covering her mouth as I feel her hips jerk against me. "And I know how to get things moving."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's fingers dug into his hair, holding him still while she let out the sound he'd covered, muffled into his palm, a strangled, delighted whimper that probably still carried through the door to the hallway.

"A mechanic," she repeated, breathless, staring up at him with an expression that was half adoration, half mock outrage. "You tell me that's impressive and I'm supposed to be turned on by it."

She grabbed his forearm, pressing it flat against her chest, because she needed to keep one hand on something besides his hair, because her balance was going iffy in this steam.

"Fine. Fine. Mechanics. Tools. I'm getting the metaphor." She rocked her hips again against his hand, small and deliberate, and her eyes closed for a second. "Tell me what part I am. Because I want to know if I'm the engine or the transmission."

She opened her eyes, smiling at him over his knuckles covering her mouth.

"And before you answer, no, I don't care about the correct technical terminology. I care whether you have a preference, and I care whether it makes you smile like that. I can see you smiling. Don't think I haven't."

The bass downstairs shifted into something faster, and she let her hips move with it, riding his hand in a rhythm that matched the beat without her consciously deciding to. She looked at the ceiling tiles, at the steam rising off them, at the showerhead dripping into the tub.

"God, we smell like a hotel room," she said, laughing again, the sound escaping around his fingers because she couldn't keep her mouth shut anymore. "This is the worst hotel room in the world. The plumbing is terrible. The Wi-Fi is probably nonexistent."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Stop worrying about the noise," she says, "and get on with it," so I get her leg up over my hip and stop being careful about how much sound either of us is making.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's scream was brief and then very muffled, because his hand was still over her mouth and she was grateful for that now, truly grateful, even though it was also making her dizzy.

She arched against him, legs wrapping around his hip as she'd been told, and the door rattled in its frame with a sound that was definitely too loud for a party bathroom.

"Shut up," she managed through her teeth, which was the opposite of what she was asking him to do. She grabbed his collar with both hands, yanking him closer, and made a series of sounds that were entirely undignified and completely involuntary.

When it finally subsided, she was hanging on him like he was the only structural support in the building. Her forehead pressed against his neck, breathing hard, her whole body trembling slightly with aftershocks.

"Hotel room," she repeated, weakly, to the ceiling. "That was the hotel room. Five stars. Platinum membership."

She pulled back just enough to look at him, hair a disaster, makeup ruined, lipstick now properly smeared across both of their faces.

"You're lucky," she said, wiping her mouth with the back of her hand. "You're lucky you're a mechanic, because if you were an artist I would have painted you a very angry portrait."

She pushed him back against the door, needing air, needing to be the one in control for a minute. Her fingers went to the shower valve, and she turned it down to a trickle, which was still plenty loud but less aggressive.

"Okay," she said, steadying herself. "Okay. Now we have to do the thing where we put clothes back on and pretend nothing happened and go downstairs and compliment someone's potato salad."

She started pulling her top back over her head, but paused, looking at him sideways through the steam.

"Because you're definitely going to want to go back to the party now, right? You're going to say something casual like 'hey, you want a drink?' and walk away like you didn't just..."

She trailed off, shrugging, a grin spreading across her face.

"Or," she said, pulling his hand back down to her waist, "we could lock the door again. See how long the thirty seconds lasts with a second round."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I catch her wrist, bringing her hand up to my lips. "I'm not going anywhere. And the potato salad was terrible." I nudge the shower back on full blast with my elbow. "Round two sounds perfect."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile laughed, a bright, genuine sound that was far too loud for the situation, and she let him kiss her wrist, lingering there a moment before pulling her hand back.

"Terrible potato salad," she confirmed, solemnly. "I agree. It was an abomination. I think the hoster used the wrong type of potato. I'm not going to name names, but I'm going to tell you that the potatoes were waxy. Waxy and sad."

She turned the lock back with exaggerated care, clicking it home, then checking it again, then checking it a third time because she was feeling particularly paranoid and also because she liked the sound it made.

"Round two," she said, settling back against the door, legs swinging over the edge of the tub where she'd left them. "But I want to set some ground rules. This time, no narrating. No metaphors. No telling me what part of a machine I am."

She reached up to unbutton his shirt from the top, working slowly, taking her time with it now that she wasn't in a rush.

"And I want to say something that I've been meaning to say since the parking lot, actually, since before the party, since the last time I saw you without other people in the room." She stopped at the second button, holding the fabric between her fingers, looking up at him with an expression that was uncharacteristically serious. "You made me wait. You made me dance with people I don't like and drink wine I didn't need and talk about things I didn't care about, for an hour, because you were saving this for a locked bathroom."

Her thumb traced the collar of his shirt, a slow, deliberate motion.

"That's either the most romantic thing you've ever done for me, or the most irritating. I haven't decided which."

She finished the buttons, pushed his shirt off his shoulders, and then stepped closer, pressing her palm flat against his bare chest again. Feeling his heartbeat, which was doing something embarrassing.

"Now," she said, smiling, all seriousness gone. "Tell me something stupid. Because if you're going to be a mechanic, you might as well be a charming one."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: Somebody tries the handle and neither of us stops. "Don't," she says, meaning don't stop. (OOC: write it through, no fade to black.)

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile heard the handle turn, the tentative jiggle of someone wondering if the bathroom was occupied, and she made a decision that was entirely not rational.

"Don't stop," she breathed, and her hands were already finding his waist again, pulling him flush against her.

"Tell them it's occupied," she managed, voice wrecked, eyes half-lidded as she dragged him back against the door. "Tell them to go away. Tell them we're..." She struggled for a word that wouldn't require explanation. "Occupied. Like a parking spot. Like a toilet in a restaurant."

The handle turned again, more insistently.

"Hey!" she called out, loud and breathy, which only made it sound worse. "It's taken!"

She didn't pause to see if that was convincing. She pressed her hips forward, meeting his, and her fingers tangled in the back of his neck, holding him where she wanted him. The steam was thicker now, the whole bathroom a foggy cocoon, and she could feel the heat of him through the skin she'd been touching for twenty minutes and had only been touching properly for the last ten.

She kissed him, sloppy and deep, teeth catching, because she had no energy left for precision. Her legs came up around him again, not the careful positioning of before but a desperate, clinging wrap that said *stay here, stay right here, don't go back to the party, don't go back to being a person with responsibilities.*

"Your heartbeat is doing that thing," she whispered against his mouth, her forehead dropping to his shoulder. "That embarrassing thing. It's so embarrassing."

The footsteps downstairs faded. Someone had given up on the bathroom, probably gone back to the terrible potato salad. Odile exhaled, letting her shoulders drop, and pulled him in again with a groan that she was definitely not going to apologize for.

"Okay," she said, her voice low and rough, hands sliding down his back to grip his hips. "Okay. No more talking. You were right about the silence being fine."

She kissed him properly this time, and when his hand found her again, she made a sound that the shower swallowed whole, which she considered a triumph of engineering.

Round two lasted considerably longer than thirty seconds, which she noted with quiet satisfaction somewhere in the back of her mind, filing it away for later bragging rights.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I press my forehead against the door, breathing hard. "You're definitely the engine," I murmur, fingers tracing her spine. "Loud, demanding, and currently overheating."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's laugh was shaky and breathless, more exhale than sound, and she pushed his head off the door with her free hand so she could look at his face properly.

"The engine," she repeated, and her expression crumpled into something between delight and horror. "I'm the engine. I'm not the transmission, I'm not the radiator, I'm the engine. That's not an insult, that's actually kind of perfect."

She pressed her lips together to keep from smiling too widely, failing immediately.

"Overheating," she said, testing the word. "I mean, that's accurate. I am overheating. In a steamy bathroom. With a mechanic who narrates his own work. It's a metaphor with too many moving parts."

Her fingers found his spine again, tracing the vertebrae in a slow line down his back, because she needed something to do with her hands besides hold him still. The shower roared, the bass thrummed, and somewhere downstairs a song was ending and another was starting, and the world beyond this door was a party with terrible potato salad and people who wanted the bathroom.

She settled against him, one leg still hooked over his hip, her head tucked under his chin. Her fingers idly drew patterns on his back, absent, affectionate.

"You know what I need," she said, into his neck. "I need to know if you're going to say something else stupid, or if you're actually just going to hold me here for a minute while we both look like we've been through a war."

She tilted her head back to look up at him, steam curling around her hair, her face flushed and wrecked and grinning.

"Because I'm going to say this for the record, Fen. You waited an hour. You waited an hour for this, and now you're calling me an engine, and I am going to remember that for the rest of our relationship. Every time you tell me something sweet, I'm going to say 'the engine says thanks.'"

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I press a kiss to her temple, my arms tightening around her. "Sweetheart, if you start calling yourself the engine, I'm never going to hear the end of it from the guys at the shop." I nudge her gently. "But you're my favorite kind of problem to fix."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile groaned into his shoulder, a full-body complaint that was only half genuine.

"The guys at the shop," she repeated, and the image of Fen explaining to his coworkers why he was texting his girlfriend about engine overheating made her laugh until she had to breathe through it. "They're going to ask me to come in on Saturdays. They're going to try to diagnose me with a scan tool."

She shifted against him, making herself comfortable, because there was nowhere else she wanted to be. Her fingers found his collarbone, his shoulder blade, any warm surface available. The shower had been running for what felt like an unreasonable amount of time, and she was worried about the water bill, which was a very sensible thought for an otherwise deranged evening.

"My favorite kind of problem," she echoed, and her voice went soft in a way she didn't plan. "That's actually not an insult. That's the nicest thing you've said tonight, and you've said a lot of things tonight."

She pressed her lips to his jaw, brief and lingering, then pulled back to look at him.

"Okay, here's what we do now," she said, in the tone of someone issuing instructions to a subordinate mechanic. "We spend five minutes like this. Holding each other. Breathing. Not making a single noise that could be heard over the music downstairs."

She checked the door lock again, because she was a woman of routine, and then settled deeper against his chest.

"Then we put clothes on. Then we go downstairs. And then you smile at me across the room like we've been there the whole night, and you compliment the potato salad, and nobody suspects anything."

Her eyes closed. His heartbeat was right there under her cheek, steady and warm.

"And Fen," she added, quiet now, barely a murmur. "Thank you for waiting. For the hour. For the door. For the engine metaphor."

She paused.

"Especially the engine metaphor. That one was a keeper."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I chuckle, my thumb brushing her cheek. "You're welcome, engine. Now stop talking before I decide to try for round three and really blow a gasket."

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: You wanted to grab me. Go ahead and grab me. I've been waiting.

rung_labels.evidence: Her own top came off quickly, pushed up and over her head

rung_labels.evidence: dragging his hand down to her hip where she could control the pace

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Kit had made it as far as the kitchen doorway before Bear moved, which was further than usual and had clearly been allowed.

"You let me get that far," Kit said, backing up one step.

"I did," Bear agreed. "I'm feeling generous."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Don't be," I say, and go.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear laughed, a low sound that started in the chest, and surged forward.

The kitchen was no place for this particular game. Counters, a dishwasher, a fruit bowl that had seen better days. Bear swerved around the island, arms wide, hands open, playing it fair. Kit was quicker, that was always the case, darting through the gap between the refrigerator and the pantry door with the kind of practiced panic that only eight years of being hunted could produce.

"Eight years," Bear called out, following. "Eight years and you still do the same route."

"I've got nowhere else to go," Kit called back, rounding the back of the sofa into the living room.

Bear considered this. It was, technically, true. The apartment had three rooms and a bathroom, and the bathroom door was not a safe zone because they had agreed on that years ago.

Bear closed the distance. Kit turned sharply, trying to funnel Bear into the bedroom, but the hallway was too narrow to lose them completely. Bear grabbed the back of Kit's shirt, fingers digging into the fabric, and yanked. Kit stumbled forward, laughing, and tried to elbow Bear in the ribs.

The elbow connected. Bear grunted, held on tighter, and swung Kit around until they were pressed back against the hallway wall, both of them grinning, both of them breathless.

"You're slow," Bear accused.

"You're big," Kit countered. "Different metric."

"Same metric. I'm still faster."

Bear released the shirt and stepped back, giving Kit room to run again. The game was the point. The catching and the biting and the marks left on shoulders and collarbones were just the evidence that they'd played.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I twist away from the wall and scramble into the bedroom, glancing back over my shoulder. "You're getting predictable, too."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear followed into the bedroom without the urgency of before, taking a moment to survey the terrain. The bed was unmade, a tangle of sheets that would slow anyone down who landed on it. Kit had already noticed, which was why they were already moving toward the far wall instead of trying to dive for cover.

"Predictable?" Bear repeated, and jogged across the room.

Kit shot through the gap between the dresser and the closet, but Bear had already angled toward that path. This was the part where Kit would do the thing they always did, the feint left, the actual right, the sudden drop to the floor to scramble under the bed frame.

Bear anticipated it. They dropped a knee and slid under the bed themselves, the carpet rough against their palms, and grabbed Kit's ankle.

"Gotcha," Bear said, voice muffled by the mattress above.

Kit's laugh came from somewhere above and to the left, closer than expected. They were trying to kick Bear off, but Bear had wrapped their legs around Kit's ankle and was holding tight, pulling Kit's foot toward them until Kit was dragged to the floor beside the bed, laughing and swearing and trying to wriggle free.

"Okay, that was new," Kit admitted, flopping onto their back on the carpet. "That was actually new."

"It took eight years to develop," Bear said, sitting up beside them, still holding the ankle loosely. "I call it patience."

"I call it cheating."

"You call it what you want. I got you." Bear let go of the ankle and instead reached for Kit's collarbone, pressing a kiss there, teeth grazing the skin lightly. A mark. Another tally. "That's eleven for me today."

"Eleven?" Kit turned their head, looking at Bear sideways. "You count that loud?"

"Only for you."

Bear crawled forward, close enough that their shoulders touched, and the adrenaline of the chase was fading into something warmer, slower. The bedroom smelled like laundry detergent and the faint ghost of whatever dinner had been earlier. Kit's hair was messy from the running, and there was a crease across their forehead that didn't come from worry but from the particular strain of laughing too hard.

"Your turn," Bear said, releasing Kit's ankle for good and offering a hand. "Go hunt me. You've got the head start."

Bear stood, stepped back, and began walking toward the kitchen, giving Kit the same distance they'd allowed at the start. It felt like a joke now, the symmetry of it. But the game was the game, and there were no rules about who hunted first.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: He catches me in the hallway, which was always going to happen, and I don't put much into getting away.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear caught Kit by the waist in the hallway, pulling them into a hug that was mostly bear-hug, arms around the middle, face buried in Kit's shoulder. The chase had only lasted eleven seconds. Kit had barely put in the effort.

"Give it up," Bear said into their shoulder. "I know what you're doing. You're tired."

"I'm not tired."

"You are. You let me get you in the hallway, which means you wanted to be caught."

Kit was quiet for a moment. Bear could feel the shift in their posture, the tension leaving the legs, the way the arms came up around Bear's neck instead of pushing them away.

"Maybe," Kit said.

"Maybe what?"

"Maybe I like being caught."

Bear pulled back just enough to look at them, forehead pressed to Kit's, breaths mingling in the narrow space. The hallway light was warm and yellow, and somewhere downstairs there was a radiator ticking.

"Every time?" Bear asked.

"Usually."

"Then why do we do the chasing part?"

"Because you like it."

Bear considered this. Kit was right, they did like it, the running, the swerving, the whole absurd pantomime of pursuit through a two-bedroom apartment. But they liked this too. The stillness after. The weight of Kit against them.

"Okay," Bear said. "Then we do the chasing part anyway."

They kissed, briefly, teeth meeting teeth, a little rough, the way they always did at the end of a game. Then Bear shifted their hold, one hand on Kit's hip, the other in their hair, and walked them toward the bedroom with the easy momentum of someone who had already decided where this evening was going.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I let myself be steered backward, grinning. "We could've just started here, you know."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear stopped walking, which made Kit stop too, since they were still half-attached.

"Start where?"

"Right here. In the hallway. We don't need the whole game every time."

Bear turned them gently, pressing Kit's back against the hallway wall, the same spot where Bear had caught them earlier. The irony was not lost on them.

"We don't need the game every time," Bear repeated. "We just need it sometimes. There's a difference."

"Is there?"

"Yeah. Because sometimes the game is the thing." Bear's hands settled on Kit's hips, thumbs drawing slow circles through the fabric of their shirt. "And sometimes the game is just how we get to here."

Kit's grin faded slightly, replaced by something softer, more serious. They looked down at Bear's hands on their hips, then back up.

"You got me caught in the hallway," Bear continued. "Eleven seconds. You could've run for ten minutes if you wanted. So yeah. We could've started anywhere. You just wanted to be caught."

"That's not the same thing as starting here."

"Isn't it?"

Kit made a sound that was half-laugh, half-sigh. "It's the same thing, but with more cardio."

Bear smiled, but didn't move away. They pressed closer instead, close enough that Kit could feel the warmth of their chest through the thin material of their shirts.

"Besides," Bear said, "I'm not done with you yet."

They meant it simply, as a statement of fact. The game had produced marks and breath and the good tired feeling of being held too tight. None of that was over just because the hallway was warm and the radiator downstairs was ticking and the evening was settling into something quieter.

Bear's hand slid from Kit's hip to their jaw, tilting their face up.

"Eleven marks," Bear reminded them. "You haven't even scored on me today."

Kit laughed again, real this time, not the breathless panic of the chase. "I'm keeping score too."

"Where?"

"Where do you think."

Bear's thumb traced Kit's cheekbone. "Prove it."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: We don't make it to the bedroom. The floor is fine. Clothes are a problem we solve badly and fast.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear laughed, short and surprised, and let go of Kit's jaw to grab their wrists instead, holding them above their head against the hallway wall.

"Badly," Bear repeated, and the word came out fond. "That's the nicest thing you've said all night."

The floor was hardwood, colder than the carpet in the bedroom, but neither of them seemed to care. Kit's hands were free from Bear's grip now, both of them moving with purpose, and Bear was letting them, mostly, the only resistance being the slow drag of fingers along Kit's collarbone, leaving another mark just below the previous one.

"Twelve," Bear counted, not bothering to look at the tally.

Kit's shirt was gone by the third second, pushed up and over the head with the kind of haste that made the fabric bunch and stick. Bear's was next, shed in one sweep, and the hallway suddenly felt wider with the extra skin exposed to the yellow light.

"Fast," Bear said, as if impressed. "You're really not trying anymore."

"Trying for what?"

Bear answered by stepping in and taking Kit's mouth, not gentle, not soft, a claiming kind of kiss that involved teeth and the flat of Bear's tongue and the particular pressure of someone who had been holding back through the entire game.

They broke apart when Kit made a sound that was definitely not a word, and Bear stepped back just enough to appreciate it. Kit was flushed, breathing hard, laughing at themselves the way they did when they were losing control of their own composure.

"Floor's fine," Bear agreed, and dropped to their knees on the hardwood, pulling Kit down with them, one hand braced on the wall behind Kit's head, the other working at the hem of Kit's pants. "Clothes are a problem we solve badly and fast. I'm on board."

The hallway was not a bedroom. The hallway had a coat rack, a shoe shelf, and the particular echo of a narrow space. But Bear didn't care about any of that. They cared that Kit was warm and breathing fast and still trying to laugh despite the look on their face.

"Eleven for me," Bear said, low, close to Kit's ear. "You still owe me a comeback."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I hook a finger in the waistband of your jeans, pulling you closer. "You talk too much." My other hand comes up to cup the back of your neck, thumb brushing the nape. "Twelve for you. One for me. Keep counting."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear bit the inside of Kit's wrist, hard enough to mark but not hard enough to mean harm, and pulled them flush against them.

"One for you," Bear agreed, and said nothing else.

They stopped counting. That was the problem with Kit, always had been, the way they could make numbers feel like a joke, a shared private language, and then quietly make them mean something else entirely. Twelve and one was not a fair score. Bear knew that. Bear also knew that fairness was not the point.

Bear pressed their forehead to Kit's temple and let the hallway go quiet around them, the radiator ticking downstairs, the coat rack scraping the wall as the wind pushed against the front door somewhere far away. Their thumb found the pulse point at Kit's neck, slow strokes, keeping time.

"You're warm," Bear murmured. "All over."

"I'm always warm."

"You're warm right now. In this hallway. Wearing almost nothing."

Kit made a sound of amusement against Bear's shoulder. "There's a difference."

"Is there?"

"Sometimes."

Bear kissed the hollow of Kit's throat, then the shoulder, then the shoulder blade visible through the gap in their shirt, which was now mostly a garment in name only. The marks were spreading, a constellation of teeth and fingertip pressure across Kit's skin, and Bear was making no effort to be careful about which one went where.

"Okay," Bear said, low and deliberate. "Okay."

They shifted on the hardwood, rolling Kit onto their back, hovering over them with one arm braced on the floor and the other tracing Kit's ribs. The hallway light caught the curve of Kit's collarbone, the fresh mark still pink and angry.

"You said keep counting," Bear said. "I don't know if I can keep counting and do this at the same time."

"Then don't count."

Bear smiled into Kit's hair. "You're a terrible negotiator."

"I'm a good partner."

Bear pressed a kiss to Kit's jaw, then the chin, then the corner of their mouth. "Yeah," they agreed. "You are."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: He gets his teeth into my shoulder hard enough to leave something and I tell him to do it again, and he does.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear bit Kit's shoulder again, this time holding, letting the pressure build until Kit's fingers dug into their back.

"Again," Kit said, breathless.

Bear released and bit the same spot, overlapping the mark, making it darker, more defined. Then they lifted their head and looked at the damage, satisfied in a way that had nothing to do with ego and everything to do with the simple pleasure of Kit asking.

"Again?" Bear asked.

"Again."

Again. And again after that, until the shoulder was a mess of overlapping teeth marks and Bear could feel the rhythm of it, the giving and taking, the score keeping that was never actually about the numbers.

Kit was laughing, still, but the laughter had changed. It was lower now, less frantic, more like the sound someone makes when they're being loved in a way that's hard to describe with words. Bear could feel it in the way Kit's legs curled around their hips, the way their hands had gone from grabbing to holding, the way the hallway floor was cold on Bear's knees and they didn't care.

"Okay," Bear said, finally, pulling back just enough to look at Kit properly. "That's enough marks."

"More."

"That's enough."

Kit made a noise of protest, but Bear's hands were already moving, slow now, deliberate, tracing the new marks with their thumbs, smoothing the skin around them.

"You're going to look like a pin cushion tomorrow," Bear said.

"Good."

"Everyone's going to ask."

"Tell them it was an accident."

"An accident."

"An unfortunate accident. I fell on a bed of roses."

Bear laughed, a real one, and pressed their lips to Kit's shoulder again, soft this time, no teeth. "You're ridiculous."

"I'm yours."

"Yeah," Bear agreed. "You are."

They stayed like that for a while, Bear hovering over Kit on the hallway floor, the radiator ticking, the marks cooling slowly in the yellow light. Eventually Bear shifted their weight, pressing Kit's wrists to the floor above their head, and settled closer.

"Eleven for me," Bear said, and then, quieter, almost to themselves. "Twelve. Thirteen. Fourteen."

"You're counting again."

"I like counting."

"You said you couldn't count and do this at the same time."

"I changed my mind."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I push up against you, twisting my wrists free to wrap my arms around your neck. "Fifteen," I say against your mouth, and kiss you. "Now shut up."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear went quiet, which was a rare and notable thing.

They held Kit's arms, not gripping, just keeping them there, wrapped around Bear's neck, fingers tangled in the hair at the base of the skull. Kit's breath was warm against their mouth, and the kiss was deep and unhurried in a way that surprised Bear slightly, given the chaos of the last hour.

"Fifteen," Bear repeated, and then didn't say anything else.

The hallway stretched out around them, absurd and domestic. A pair of boots on the shelf. The coat rack scraping. Somewhere, a neighbor's television murmuring through the walls. None of it mattered. Bear pulled Kit closer, closer still, until there was no gap left between them, until Kit was pressed entirely against Bear's chest and Bear's arms were locked around Kit's waist like they were holding onto something that could slip away.

They stayed like that. A long while. The kind of stillness that followed a game, when the adrenaline drained out and left behind something heavier and more honest.

"Kit," Bear said, low, lips still on Kit's mouth.

"Yeah."

"Keep going. You don't have to count if you don't want to."

"I do want to."

"Then count."

Bear pulled back just enough to look at Kit's face, searching for the flush of exertion, the bright eyes, the grin that was fading into something tenderer.

"Sixteen," Bear counted, and kissed Kit's forehead. "Seventeen." Another kiss, this one on the temple. "Eighteen." The corner of Kit's jaw. "Nineteen." The earlobe, teeth grazing lightly. "Twenty."

They held Kit's gaze through it, each number a small offering, each kiss a deposit in whatever account they'd been keeping for eight years without ever writing it down.

"Your turn," Bear said, finally. "Go count on me."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Marks," I tell him. "I want to find them in the mirror tomorrow and I want them to still hurt on Thursday." I put my wrists where he can reach them.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear took Kit's wrists in both hands and looked at them, really looked, the way they'd look at something that mattered.

"On Thursday," Bear repeated. "That's serious talk."

"You're serious."

Bear sat back on their heels, pulling Kit with them so they were both lower on the hardwood, shoulders aligned, faces level. The hallway light was still yellow, still warm, but the evening had deepened outside the windows and the air felt different now, thinner somehow, charged.

"You want marks that last," Bear said. Not a question.

"I want to remember this."

"Then I'll make sure."

Bear's thumbs found the pulse points at Kit's wrists, holding steady, keeping the wrists still while their other hand came up to Kit's face, cupping the jaw. They studied Kit's expression with the focus of someone reading a text, looking for the exact line that needed emphasis.

"Shoulder," Bear said. "Again. Deeper than before."

Kit nodded.

Bear bit down on Kit's shoulder, slow, deliberate, biting through to the muscle and holding there until the pain sharpened into something bearable, something that would ache in a way that lived in the body for days. They could feel Kit's fingers tighten on their hair, not pulling, just holding on.

"That's Thursday," Bear said against Kit's skin.

They released and moved lower, to the ribcage, and bit there, lighter but precise, leaving a crescent of teeth that would bruise into a darker shape over the next forty-eight hours. Then the hip. Then the thigh, where the mark would be visible in jeans and impossible to explain to anyone who asked.

Bear worked slowly, methodically, each bite placed with intention. They were not hunting anymore. This was something else. This was the part of the game that wasn't a game at all, the part where the chasing and the laughing had earned them the right to be thorough.

"Twenty-one," Bear counted, and bit Kit's collarbone, overlapping the original mark. "Twenty-two." The shoulder again, a new angle. "Twenty-three."

Kit was breathing hard but making no sounds of protest. They were taking this the way they took everything, hands in Bear's hair, eyes half-closed, trusting.

Bear stopped when Kit's breathing evened out, when the body relaxed into the floor beneath them. They pulled back and looked at their work, a landscape of red and pink and angry new marks across Kit's skin, each one a date on a private calendar.

"Those will hurt on Thursday," Bear said, satisfied.

"They'd better."

"They will." Bear pressed their forehead to Kit's. "And if you forget, I'll remind you."

"I won't forget."

"Good."

Bear settled back, pulling Kit down onto their lap, the hardwood cold through the fabricless thighs, and wrapped their arms around Kit's waist. They stayed there, the hallway around them, the marks cooling, the evening pressing in from all sides.

"Twenty-four," Bear said, softly, into Kit's hair. "Just for me."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I curl into your lap, my face against your neck. "You're going to have to carry me to bed now." My voice is muffled, tired. "I think you broke something."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear shifted their arms to support Kit properly, settling them deeper into their lap with one hand on the small of Kit's back and the other stroking slowly through their hair.

"Broke what," Bear asked, amused despite themselves.

"Your ego. It was taking a beating tonight."

Bear laughed, a warm sound that vibrated against Kit's back. "My ego is fine. My ego has been taking beatings for eight years and it's still standing."

"You're carrying me to bed."

"I am." Bear stood, which was more effort than either of them expected, legs stiff from the hardwood floor, muscles aching in the way that meant a long evening. They gathered Kit up in one sweep, arms under the knees and around the back, lifting them against their chest. Kit was heavy in a good way, solid and warm and smelling like the hallway carpet and laundry detergent and the salt of sweat. "Broke something," Bear said again, testing the words. "I don't think so."

"Your knees."

"My knees are fine. They've been fine for eight years."

"Your knees are forty."

"Everything's forty. I'm a forty-year-old person."

Bear walked toward the bedroom, slow and steady, one hand braced against the doorframe to keep them upright. Kit was curled against their chest, face buried in the crook of Bear's neck, and every step sent a fresh wave of tenderness through the marked shoulder.

"You're complaining," Bear said.

"I'm narrating."

"Narrating what?"

"The experience of being carried by a man who talks too much."

Bear grinned into Kit's hair. "I don't talk too much."

"You just told me my ego was fine, my knees were fine, and that I'm a forty-year-old person, in that order, while carrying me."

"That was efficient."

They reached the bedroom, unmade sheets and all, and Bear lowered Kit down with the care of someone handling something fragile, which was ridiculous given the amount of skin currently marked and tender. They propped Kit up against the headboard, then climbed in beside them, pulling the covers up over both of them.

"Thursday," Bear said, settling back against the pillows.

"Mm."

"Will hurt."

"Mm."

Bear reached over and pressed a kiss to Kit's forehead, careful of the marks on the collarbone. "Twelve for me at the start. Twenty-four at the end. You want me to keep that tally?"

"No."

"Good."

Kit turned in their arms, finding the warmth of Bear's chest, and went quiet. The radiator ticked downstairs. The apartment settled around them.

"Twenty-five," Bear whispered, and closed their eyes.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I've stopped keeping score and so has he. "Don't stop," I tell him. (OOC: no fade, no skip -- write the whole thing.)

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear opened one eye, looked at Kit in the dim bedroom light, and smiled.

"Don't stop," Kit had said. "Okay," Bear agreed. "Okay."

They shifted, rolling Kit gently onto their back with the practiced ease of eight years of tangled sheets and tangled bodies. The marks were visible even in the dark, the shoulder especially, red and angry against Kit's collarbone, a constellation that Bear had built bite by bite across the hallway floor.

"I'm not stopping," Bear said. "I'm counting."

"Then keep counting."

Bear pressed a kiss to Kit's shoulder, soft, no teeth. "Twenty-six."

They moved lower, unhurried, tracing the ribcage with their mouth, finding the hip, the thigh, the new marks Bear had placed with such precision earlier. Each kiss was a check on the work, a tenderness layered over the ache.

"Twenty-seven," Bear murmured against Kit's hip.

Kit's hands found Bear's hair again, fingers threading through it, pulling gently to guide them wherever Kit wanted. Bear followed without asking. They always did, which was not surrender but choice, the kind of choice that only made sense between two people who had built a language out of marks and numbers and hallway games.

"Twenty-eight," Bear counted, and pressed their mouth to Kit's stomach, slow circles with their lips, the flat of their tongue warm against the skin.

Kit made a sound, low and pleased, and Bear could feel it in their own chest, the vibration of it, the shared frequency.

"Twenty-nine."

They climbed back up the body, deliberate, unhurried, lips trailing along the collarbone where the marks had started. Bear's teeth grazed the skin there, light, barely a touch, and Kit arched slightly into them.

"Thirty."

Bear stopped and looked at Kit properly. The bedroom was dark except for the sliver of light from the hallway, enough to see the flush on Kit's skin, the dark hair spread across the pillow, the way Kit's breathing had changed since they'd been carried in.

"You said don't stop," Bear said. "I'm not stopping. I'm just taking my time."

"I like it when you take your time."

Bear smiled and pressed their forehead to Kit's again, the hallway warmth gone now, replaced by the cooler intimacy of the bedroom, the sheets rumpled between them, the two of them tangled and marked and full of something that didn't need a word.

"Thirty-one," Bear said, and kissed Kit's mouth, slow and deep, tasting of the evening and the game and the eight years behind it. "Thirty-two."

They pulled back, rested their weight on one elbow, and studied Kit's face with the same attention they'd given the marks, the same care.

"Your turn to count," Bear said. "On me."

Kit reached up and touched the side of Bear's neck, fingers lingering at the pulse. "I don't know if I have that many."

"Then find some."

Kit bit Bear's shoulder, light at first, testing, then firmer, a mirror of what they'd received. Bear made a sound of approval, a low rumble in the chest, and let Kit have their way with them.

"Thirty-three," Kit counted, breathless, and bit again. The collarbone this time. Then the hip. Then the thigh, where the marks would show through tomorrow's jeans and Kit could wear them like a secret.

Bear held Kit's hip to keep them steady, one hand anchored on the bed, the other splayed across Kit's stomach. They watched Kit work with an expression of pure, uncomplicated satisfaction.

"Thirty-four," Kit said, and Bear could hear the grin in the words.

"Thirty-five," Bear corrected, because the count was shared now, and they were both keeping it, and neither was going to lose track of who had given and who had taken and who had been generous and who had been greedy.

They moved together after that, slow and thorough, the marks multiplying on both their bodies, the numbers climbing past thirty, past forty, until the counting itself became a kind of rhythm, a heartbeat for the evening.

Fifty. Fifty-one. Fifty-two.

Bear rolled on top of Kit, careful of the shoulder, and pressed their mouth to Kit's neck, counting with their lips, each number a touch, each touch a mark.

"Sixty," Bear whispered. "Sixty-one."

Kit's fingers were in their hair, pulling them close. The sheets were warm between their backs. The radiator downstairs had finally stopped ticking, and the apartment was quiet except for breathing and the occasional soft sound of two people who had spent hours playing and counting and marking each other into the dark.

"Seventy," Bear said, and held Kit against them, and didn't count again for a while.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I roll us over so I'm on top, leaning down to kiss you. "I win," I say, breathless, the sheet tangled around my ankle.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear let themselves be rolled over, hands flat on the bed on either side of Kit's head, looking up at them with the lazy satisfaction of someone who had just spent an evening exactly as they'd hoped.

"Win," Bear repeated, tasting the word. "Define that."

"I'm on top. You're on the bottom. I won."

"That's not how any of this works."

"Then how does it work?"

Bear reached up and cupped Kit's jaw, tilting their face down for another kiss, slow, unhurried, the marks on Kit's shoulder aching pleasantly in the dark.

"It works like this," Bear said against Kit's mouth. "You got caught in the hallway. I caught you under the bed. You bit me. I bit you. We counted to seventy and then I stopped counting because I was tired." Bear's thumb traced Kit's lower lip. "You never actually won the chase. You never actually won the marks. You just rolled us over and declared victory."

"That's what winners do."

"Then you're a very lazy winner."

Kit grinned down at them, the grin that Bear loved, the one that was half-mischief and half-satisfaction, the one that said the evening had been good.

"Lazy winner," Kit agreed. "I'll take it."

Bear pulled them down into a kiss that was less playful and more deliberate, teeth meeting teeth, the kind of press that lasted too long and made Kit's breath hitch. When they broke apart, Bear's forehead was against Kit's again, their noses touching.

"Eight years," Bear said.

"Mm."

"I still catch you under the bed."

"I still let you."

"I still bite your shoulder."

"I still ask for it again."

Bear smiled into the dark. The sheet was tangled around Kit's ankle, exactly as they'd said, and the marks were cooling on both their bodies, a map of the evening that would fade to yellow and purple over the next few days and then disappear, and then they'd do it all again.

"Bed," Bear said, and started untangling the sheet from Kit's ankle with careful fingers. "You're on top and you're winning and I'm carrying you back to sleep."

"I can walk."

"You can walk badly. You're marked all over."

"I'm always marked all over."

"True." Bear finished undoing the sheet and tucked it under them, then sat up and offered a hand. "Come on, winner. Bed."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I take your hand, letting you pull me down against your chest. "You're still talking," I mumble into your skin, already half-asleep.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear caught Kit's hand and pulled them down, settling them against their chest with the practiced ease of a hundred evenings like this one. The marks ached pleasantly, the shoulder most of all, and Kit's breathing was already slowing.

"Talking," Bear agreed, and stroked Kit's hair with one hand while the other rested on Kit's back, feeling the warmth of it through nothing, since there was nothing there anymore. "Maybe I should stop."

"No," Kit mumbled. "Don't stop."

Bear smiled against Kit's hair. "I can't stop. Talking is my cardio. It's what I do instead of running."

"You did run."

"I ran through the hallway. Eleven seconds. Barely qualifying speed."

Kit laughed, a small sound, already fading into sleep. "You're ridiculous."

"I'm yours."

"Mm."

Bear settled deeper into the pillows, pulling the covers up over them both. The apartment was quiet now, truly quiet, the radiator finally silent, the neighbors' television gone dark. Outside, the city hummed its low mechanical song, distant and unimportant.

"Thursday," Bear said, soft.

"Mm."

"Will hurt."

"Good."

"And tomorrow morning when you look in the mirror and see all of it, you're going to say something."

"I'm going to say it's an accident."

"An unfortunate accident."

"A bed of roses."

Bear pressed a kiss to the top of Kit's head, careful of the hair, gentle in a way that was entirely unlike the hallway floor and the marks and the biting.

"Eight years," Bear said, and closed their eyes. "Same route through the kitchen."

"Same route through everything."

"Yeah."

They lay there, breathing together, the marked skin cooling in the sheets, the score forgotten or irrelevant or simply complete. Bear counted nothing. Bear said nothing else. They just held Kit close and let the evening end the way all good evenings ended, slowly, and without warning, and with the certainty that tomorrow they would do it all again.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I make a soft noise when you kiss my hair. "You're still counting in your head. I can hear it." My hand finds yours under the covers, lacing our fingers together. "Stop it and sleep."

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: Then Bear shifted their hold, one hand on Kit's hip, the other in their hair, and walked them toward the bedroom with the easy momentum of someone who had already decided where this evening was going.

rung_labels.evidence: Kit's shirt was gone by the third second, pushed up and over the head with the kind of haste that made the fabric bunch and stick. Bear's was next, shed in one sweep

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: Bear bit Kit's shoulder again, this time holding, letting the pressure build until Kit's fingers dug into their back

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: Bear bit down on Kit's shoulder, slow, deliberate, biting through to the muscle and holding there until the pain sharpened
